etl_receipts.label: ETL receipts
etl_receipts.summary: The paperwork behind each row: what was read to make it, how the processing went, and what was kept out of the table's columns.
etl_receipts.grain: One receipt for each row of a table that has receipts, plus one for each record that was read and recorded without becoming a row.
etl_receipts.selection: A table and its receipts are published together as one build. Read both from the same entry of the publication index; a receipts file from another build does not match the table's rows.

columns.description: This receipt's own fingerprint: a SHA-256 digest of all its other columns, so a receipt that was changed or damaged no longer matches its id.
The table this receipt belongs to, by name (`crs_reports`). A few datasets have no table of their own and exist only as receipts.
Version of the rule that says which of the table's fields are published as columns and which are kept in the receipt.
The build that published this receipt. A table and its receipts are always published together as one build, and this names it.
A SHA-256 fingerprint of the table's name and the row's key. Empty on a receipt that states no key.
A SHA-256 fingerprint of the row's published values. It changes when any of them changes, which ties a receipt to one exact version of its row. Empty on a receipt that has no row.
The row's key: each key column's name and its value, in the typed form shown under "How to find the receipt for a row". Empty on a receipt that states no key.
Which processing attempt produced the receipt. A failed attempt, and one that produced no row, have one too.

`accepted`: the record became the row this receipt goes with. `observed`: something was read and recorded, and no row goes with it (a dataset that has no table, a read that produced no row, or a row since removed). `rejected`, `refused` or `error`: the record did not become a row, and none was made up for it; each table's pipeline chooses among the three words. All five describe our processing, never the publisher's own status for the record.
Name and version of the program, or reading rule, that produced the receipt.

columns.column_type: STRUCT(source_id VARCHAR, source_uri VARCHAR, sha256 VARCHAR, locator VARCHAR, body_version VARCHAR)[]
columns.description: What was read to produce the receipt, in order, a source read twice listed twice. For each: its identifier (`source_id`), its address (`source_uri`), a SHA-256 fingerprint of its content (`sha256`), the place within it (`locator`) and, for a stored copy, which copy (`body_version`). Every receipt names at least one source, with a fingerprint or a stored-copy version.

The fields this table keeps out of its columns, by name, in the typed form shown under "How to read a value out of a receipt". For many tables that is the whole record as the pipeline held it before conversion (`raw_record`); for others, named fields such as a source link. On a receipt for a record that did not become a row, it holds the fields that were read.
Notes about the processing itself, in the same typed form, such as which earlier build's receipt for this row was carried forward and what that receipt held.

The 2026-09-21 fork date check across all 2,001,531 rows found 52,699 posted_date
values before 1990, including eight in year 0000; one value was in the future,
2,020 were missing and no other values were uncastable. Source date values remain

consumer audit, 1,854,836 documents resolve to published dockets; 466 preserve unmatched
literal links across 137 docket IDs, and 146,229 have NULL links. The 348

Calendar searches must distinguish source dates from instants. Under the
Regulations.gov convention in SpicyDocs' `regulations_gov_day`, date-only
values and bare `T00:00:00Z` retain their printed day; other offset-bearing
timestamps use `America/New_York`, not their UTC date. For example,
`2026-10-05T03:59:59Z` is October 4 at 23:59:59 EDT, while
`2026-11-24T04:59:59Z` is November 23 at 23:59:59 EST. This bare-midnight
exception is source-specific, not a rule for arbitrary timestamps.

This guarded DuckDB example selects October 2–16 inclusive in Eastern
calendar days (not a 14-day instant interval). It handles the shown ISO
forms, preserving the source's date-only convention; year zero, malformed
values and offset-free timestamps yield NULL. Inspect those unknowns
separately rather than treating exclusion from the filter as no deadline.
Do not compare UTC timestamp strings with a date-only upper bound.

```sql
WITH calendar AS (
  SELECT document_id,
    CASE
      WHEN left(v, 4) = '0000' THEN NULL
      WHEN regexp_full_match(v, '[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}(T00:00:00Z)?')
        THEN TRY_CAST(left(v, 10) AS DATE)
      WHEN regexp_full_match(v, '[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T.+(Z|[+-][0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2})')
        THEN CAST(TRY_CAST(v AS TIMESTAMPTZ) AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York' AS DATE)
    END AS end_day
  FROM (SELECT document_id, trim(comment_end_date) AS v FROM documents)
)
SELECT document_id, end_day FROM calendar
WHERE end_day >= DATE '2026-10-02' AND end_day < DATE '2026-10-17';
```

A date field alone does not establish submission purpose or the legally
controlling/current deadline. For example, FR 2026-15634's DATES text
specifies October 2, 2026 objections/hearing requests under 40 CFR part 178,
not ordinary comments. NULL does not establish that no deadline exists.
Read the notice's filing instructions and later notices before acting.
`fr_docket_links` offers source docket navigation; `comment_periods` offers
derived date-window candidates, not a complete legal extension history.

Rows are additive. The Mirrulations mirror keeps every capture and never
sees a deletion, so a posting Regulations.gov later removes, or moves to
another docket, stays here: on 2026-10-03 FNA-2026-0301-0004, the Utah
notice (FR 2026-18893) filed to the Idaho docket, answered 404 while this
table held it with `withdrawn = 'false'`; Regulations.gov had re-posted it
as FNA-2026-0313-0006, and its four comments appear under both. A daily
step lists every docket with a document posted or modified in the past
week and reads by id each held document the listing omits:
`publisher_status` is `removed` where Regulations.gov answers 404 or 410.
Older dockets are not checked, so NULL means never checked, not still
published. Removed rows stay here; `agency_stats`, `feed_summary`,
`agency_monthly_volume` and `discovery_signals` leave them and their
comments out. Filter `publisher_status IS DISTINCT FROM 'removed'` to do
the same.

classes.label: Public comments
classes.summary: One posted public-comment record, linked to its stated docket and parent document when those references are supplied. Null docket references remain in the table and agency totals. Attachments, source text and extraction results are separate observations; missing text or file URLs do not prove the publisher received no attachment. Agency-partitioned publication supports scoped record queries.
classes.coverage: True range, floored and open-ended. Posted dates are stated from 1990-01-01 rather than from the raw minimum of year 0000, on the same publisher defect as `documents`; the mirror is rebuilt from the catalog, so the latest posted date is a query (`SELECT max(posted_date)`), not a stated bound. See the data-quality note.
classes.data_quality: Rows with a `posted_date` before 1990 carry the same publisher defect as `documents` (`WHERE posted_date < '1990'` counts them); filter on the date when recency matters. A comment on a posting Regulations.gov removed stays here, and where the publisher moved the posting it re-posted the comments under new ids, so one comment can appear twice: on 2026-10-03 FNA-2026-0301-0006 to -0009, on the removed FNA-2026-0301-0004, are FNA-2026-0313-0002 to -0005, body for body. `agency_stats` and `feed_summary` leave them out; to do the same, keep rows `WHERE comment_on_document_id IS NULL OR comment_on_document_id NOT IN (SELECT document_id FROM documents WHERE publisher_status = 'removed')`.

classes.label: Public comment counts

Each row counts the comments of one agency, docket and posting month, so consumers can compute comment totals without scanning the full table. It is rebuilt from the same catalog snapshot as each comments publication. Its rows are groups, not files: no Parquet file exists per row. Months are posting months: an agency posts in batches, so a spike here dates postings, and `comments.receive_date`, the agency's stated receipt date, dates receipt.
classes.coverage: Derived. Counts over `comments` by agency, docket and posting month; it covers exactly what that table covers and adds no rows of its own.
classes.data_quality: Its counts include the comments held on a posting Regulations.gov removed (see `comments`), which `agency_stats` and `feed_summary` subtract. To subtract them yourself, count those rows in `comments` by agency, docket and posting month.

classes.coverage: Derived. One row per docket over `dockets`, `documents` and `comments`; it covers exactly what those cover.

classes.coverage: Derived. Totals over `dockets`, `documents` and `comments`; it covers exactly what those cover.

Built by `build_agency_monthly_volume` from document `posted_date`; missing, uncastable and year-zero dates are omitted.
classes.coverage: Derived from `documents`: counts by agency, month and document type. Excludes NULL, uncastable and year-zero dates and publisher-removed postings. classes.summary: One Federal Register docket-reference occurrence, preserving printed docket labels and explicit Regulations.gov links separately. `link_source` names the source; repeated printed labels remain distinct. Printed agency labels are not automatically Regulations.gov identities. Qualified normalization candidates stay visible. Rulemaking grouping uses printed or both-source references only. Main Register number/date and docket values support exact navigation.

classes.label: Agency activity spikes
classes.summary: Per-agency document-output spike signal that powers the feed's discovery panel — agencies whose document count in the trailing 30 days is at least 2× their prior-year monthly mean, requiring ≥24 documents in the prior year to suppress tiny-denominator noise. Recomputed relative to the run date, so rows turn over on every rebuild; it is a current-state signal, not a time series. Built by `build_discovery_signals` from `documents`, less postings Regulations.gov removed (`documents.publisher_status`).
classes.coverage: Not a range. A dated snapshot recomputed from `documents` at each build. Its date is the calculation instant the file's metadata records (`spicy_regs.discovery_signals.as_of`, beside the date policy and the `documents` digest it read; `parquet_kv_metadata` on the generation's file returns them), not `measured_on`, which dates the audit of this note. Future dates are excluded from recent activity. This is not a historical series or a complete measure of agency activity. Receipt: fork-execution-2026-09-21/discovery-utc/MANUAL-AUDIT.md.
classes.data_quality: Activity windows use UTC instants and preserve explicit source offsets. Dates and timestamps without offsets use UTC; source values remain unchanged. Corpus backfills and source date anomalies can affect these document-count signals.

Annual-edition section metadata from the 2025 edition and, for some titles, the 2026 edition (`SELECT DISTINCT edition_year, title` lists which), not full publication history or body text. classes.label: Congressional bills
classes.summary: One bill or resolution. Full BILLSTATUS records, older API details and retained archive-list rows provide different amounts of detail. Pre-108th detail records do not include walked action, committee, text, subject or related-bill lists; their missing values stay NULL. `cosponsor_count` is retained when stated. Without actions, stage and signed-date rules remain unset. Main identifiers support navigation; source method and processing evidence are inspected separately.
classes.coverage: True range on the archive index, mixed on enrichment. The index reaches the earliest Congresses, with latest actions from 1799-12-16. Scoped bill-family runs enrich the 108th Congress onward from GovInfo BILLSTATUS and the 82nd–107th from Congress.gov details. Older list-only rows can remain where enrichment has not run. Missing child records or CBO estimates do not prove source absence.
classes.data_quality: **Historical cosponsor-count defect:** the 2026-09-21 native-XML audit found 13,154 wrong zero counts in the then-retained 118th Congress HR/S output using SpicyDocs 0.24.2. The current reader counts the publisher's separate cosponsors list, including withdrawn entries, as the column description states. Corrected code does not establish that every historical row has been re-read; consult the selected generation's audit before claiming population-wide repair. Historical receipt: `legislative-release-candidate-2026-09-21/`. `statutes_at_large_cite` is filled at this table's merge by joining the published `laws` table on `bill_id`, as its column sentence says: `bill-family` reads `laws` best-effort after its merge and takes the law's citation where one is published, keeping a citation already here where `laws` has none for the bill; with no `laws` table published the column stays as it was, NULL on a cold start. It is never guessed: `laws` publishes a citation only from a captured PLAW USLM file, and reads a NULL through its own `uslm_outcome`. `public_law_number` and `law_type` are not that case: they come from the bill's own publisher record — its `laws` entry, when the publisher states one — and are filled wherever the bill family has reached. `url_source` `congress_api_list` marks a row the retired list writer last wrote. Its run of 2026-09-23 replaced 3,044 BILLSTATUS `update_date` instants with the list route's same-day dates and 3,095 congress.gov page URLs with API resource URLs (receipt `drift-audit-2026-09-23/`). The bill family re-reads every such bill in its scope instead of skipping it as unchanged, so the current Congress's rows heal on its next run; the 47 rows it relabelled in the 114th–118th (five of the replaced URLs among them) are re-read only by a run scoped to their Congress. `update_date` merges by the larger value, so a re-read never moves it backwards; the 46 rows of the 119th (and 42 older) whose list date is later than BILLSTATUS's therefore keep that date-only value after the re-read, and until BILLSTATUS catches up they read `url_source` `billstatus` beside an `update_date` no BILLSTATUS document stated. Each run reads stage and signing date again from the stored actions, so a rule change needs no re-read. The 26 BILLSTATUS bills of the 108th-111th and 117th that stayed in doubt after every read on 2026-09-29 list a printing twice or without a type, so their `version_count` exceeds their `bill_versions` rows.

classes.label: Bill policy areas and legislative subjects
classes.summary: One policy-area and subject-list assignment per bill, from Congress.gov or GovInfo BILLSTATUS. Join on `bill_id`. Subject names are filter values, not separate bill records. Native rows use `subjects`; legacy rows use `subjects_json`. Acquisition method and time belong to receipts for native rows; legacy rows retain `carrier` and `enriched_at`.
classes.coverage: Sampled. Subject assignments for bills from the 93rd Congress onward. From the 108th, assignments come from held BILLSTATUS rows or bulk archives; earlier bills and refused bulk records use the keyed Congress.gov API, up to 2,000 a run. Bulk reads cover 32 folders per run, newest first; no new request starts after 20 minutes. Missing bills may be pending, refused or outside the run's scope.
classes.data_quality: A missing row can mean pending, failed or outside the configured scope. An empty assignment can mean no assignments or that the source did not hold the requested bill; those outcomes are not separately represented in this table. Rows copied from the bill family are rewritten when the family's BILLSTATUS read changes; other answers are not asked again. The table does not retain the original response or its digest.

classes.label: Planned agency actions
classes.summary: One row per Regulation Identifier Number (RIN) per agenda edition, ingested from the OIRA/OMB Unified Agenda published at reginfo.gov by `build_unified_agenda`. A Tier-1 rulemaking-lifecycle source: the upstream, forward-looking catalog of rulemakings agencies *plan* to pursue, keyed by the same `rin` that appears in `federal_register` (`regulation_id_numbers`). Primary / dedup key is (`rin`, `agenda_edition`).
classes.coverage: True range: the retained published baseline starts at 199510 and excludes the 2004 editions and spring 2012; agenda_edition names each included edition. A local source-only replay now recovers the two 2004 editions through narrowly qualified repairs; that candidate has not been published. See docs/unified-agenda-retained-rebuild.md for the qualification boundary. A rule has one row per edition that lists it, so count distinct rin, not rows, for a number of rules.

classes.label: Docket, CFR and agenda links
classes.summary: One observed link between a Regulations.gov docket, a CFR part or a Unified Agenda RIN, with its source evidence class. Missing and ambiguous references remain unresolved. Action-notice citation rows can have both targets NULL. RIN navigation returns agenda editions; it does not merge proceedings. Main identifiers carry the relationship; receipts retain interpretation evidence.
classes.coverage: Derived, and bounded by its inputs: `dockets`, `documents`, `federal_register` and `fr_docket_links` as the live snapshot's manifest pins them.

classes.label: Rulemaking proceedings
classes.summary: One rulemaking proceeding with its source dockets, Register documents and staged events. RINs provide agenda evidence and never merge dockets. Withdrawn Regulations.gov postings supply no event, title, agency or RIN evidence. A docket-less proceeding is one Register document. `proceeding_id` continues across generations when source records overlap; main IDs link agenda associations, comment periods and lifecycle records.
classes.coverage: Derived, and bounded by its inputs (`dockets`, `documents`, `federal_register`, `fr_docket_links` and `rule_targets`) and the prior snapshot it continues ids from. A proceeding is docketed, or docket-less when it is a single Register document.

classes.label: Regulatory Agenda items
classes.summary: One row per Regulation Identifier Number: the durable Regulatory Agenda item a RIN identifies, with how many proceedings evidence links it to and whether its scope is resolved. Keyed `agenda_item_id` (`urn:rkaf:us:rin:<rin>`), one per `rin`; joined by `agenda_item_proceedings` on `agenda_item_id`, and to `unified_agenda` on `rin`. Built by `build_regulatory_agenda`.
classes.coverage: Derived, and bounded by its inputs: every RIN that `unified_agenda`, `dockets`, `documents` or `federal_register` states.

classes.label: Agenda item to proceeding links
classes.summary: One row per piece of evidence that an agenda item tracks a proceeding: a docket, Regulations.gov document or Register document that directly reports the RIN for that proceeding. Unified Agenda equality alone never links an action. Keyed `relationship_id`; joins `regulatory_agenda_items` on `agenda_item_id`, `proceedings` on `proceeding_id` and `unified_agenda` on `rin`. Built by `build_regulatory_agenda`; all columns are VARCHAR.
classes.coverage: Derived, and bounded by its inputs: `dockets`, `documents` and `federal_register` records that state a RIN the proceeding holds.

classes.label: Derived submission-date windows
classes.summary: One rule-derived group of source-reported comment windows. Extension/reopening language links windows only when an explicit page citation or qualified RIN uniquely identifies an overlapping or adjoining earlier notice. Conflicts do not link; a gap starts another period. These are candidate groupings, not verified legal extensions. Docket/proceeding anchors never merge groups, and synthetic Federal Register feed dockets anchor none. Ordered source references support navigation.
classes.coverage: Derived, and bounded by its inputs: every `federal_register` record with a `comments_close_on`, every `documents` row with a comment end date, and every Register record such a document copies lands in exactly one period, anchored or not. Left out are windows that close before they open, placeholder closes (see data quality), and legacy Regulations.gov documents that state a comment end but neither a comment start nor a posting date (all closing by 2011); the builder logs each count. Live row counts come from `describe_table`.
classes.data_quality: For date-range discovery, test all three date columns (`close_date`, `register_close_date` and `regulations_gov_close_date`). They can concern different purposes, including comments, replies, objections, hearings or petitions; the builder does not classify legal submission purpose. `close_date` is the maximum normalized close among grouped records, not the legally controlling/current deadline. The source-specific columns retain each source's maximum; a difference is not resolved by choosing the later value. Base Federal Register dates remain historical statements of each dated publication, not current status, and Regulations.gov records can update independently. Inspect source filing instructions and later notices; neither title matching nor a shared docket/RIN proves legal effect. Extension/correction documents with NULL dates can exist outside these windows, and NULL does not establish no deadline. A close on or after 2050-01-01 is a placeholder and states nothing: the inputs hold no close from 2033 to 2049, and every later one is a stand-in (Regulations.gov's 2099 and 2100 dates, FDA's 2050-02-21 open dockets, Register year typos such as 3008 for 2008). A record whose only close is a placeholder, or whose window closes before it opens, adds no dates; it is listed only as its notice's Register record when a copy states a window. The formal rulespec export is the anchored rows (`anchor_kind <> 'none'`), since rulespec's CommentPeriod needs a proceeding or docket anchor; no export exists yet. A Regulations.gov document is a notice's copy only when its `fr_doc_num` says so, so a copy that omits it stands as its own notice: on the 2026-09-28 inputs about 2,950 such documents share a docket, close day and opening (within three days) with a Register notice. An extension stays its own period when it names its notice by neither page nor RIN, when its title says "extension of time for comments" (the title matcher misses that phrasing), or when its page or RINs name more than one open notice: one extension of two proposals (2022-13209 extends 2022-08993 and 2022-08994 under RINs 0910-AI28 and 0910-AI60) links to neither. A legacy Regulations.gov document whose posting date is decades early (see `documents`) opens its period that early.

classes.label: Rulemaking lifecycles
classes.summary: One docketed proceeding's proposal-to-final history and survival outcome. The earliest Register-dated proposal takes precedence over an upload-dated proposal; the final must follow it strictly. Other events determine the outcome or censor date. Docket-less Register records cannot pair and are excluded. Unified Agenda status and routine strata remain separate context. These are docketed proceedings, not a count of distinct RINs or regulations.
classes.coverage: Derived, and bounded by its inputs: every docketed proceeding, paired from its cleaned `lifecycle_events` and censored at the day its inputs end.
classes.data_quality:
A Regulations.gov document that states no Register number in `fr_doc_num`, or whose stated number resolves to no Register row, is dated by its upload, which for a legacy document can be years after the rule: on snapshot_9b2c770e's inputs 262 lifecycles anchor on such a document, 74 of them upload pairs outside survival (docs/ontology.md). A proposal typed only by Regulations.gov (`lifecycle_events.source = 'regulations_gov'`, an unnumbered upload) can be a petition for rulemaking, a state program submission or an information-collection notice the Register files under another type: on snapshot_62318069's inputs 515 survival lifecycles since 2015 anchor on one (352 open); a Register number its title names is not read as its identity. Where the proceeding also holds the Register's proposal, the Register's anchors (54d); an upload keeps its anchor when a final falls between the two or the Register's is a comment-period extension or correction, so an earlier proposal whose Register copy is missing may still anchor on its later re-proposal (FDA's 1978 OTC-monograph dockets re-proposed in the 1990s). A final that finalizes another docket's proposal is paired in its own proceeding only and the proposal stays `open`: a RIN never groups dockets (56a), and the Register's docket labels are often an agency's own (2026-15833 names 'CMS-1849-F and CMS-0062-F' and no RIN). A Register proposal naming several dockets anchors one lifecycle per docket (502 proposals behind 2,358 of 35,327 survival rows on snapshot_62318069's inputs; EPA 20%). A posting Regulations.gov flags withdrawn (`documents.withdrawn`) anchors nothing: it was misfiled, duplicated, moved or replaced, and the Register publishes an agency's withdrawal of a rule as a document of its own.
For `routine_family` `pesticide_tolerance` the proposal is usually EPA's notice that it received a pesticide petition (FFDCA 408(d)(3)), typed Proposed Rule, not a proposal of rule text: 443 of the 459 EPA tolerance lifecycles proposed since 2020 on snapshot_448e6d9a's inputs. Time to final then runs from the receipt notice, and `proposal_form` does not tell the two apart.
FDA's notices that it filed a food or color additive petition ("Filing of Food Additive Petition", "… Color Additive Petition") are the same case with no stratum: the Register types them Proposed Rule (its `action`, "Notification of petition.", is not carried by `federal_register`), `routine_family` is NULL, and on snapshot_55d396ee's inputs 64 of the 199 FDA lifecycles proposed since 2018, and 130 of the 831 in the published FDA cell, anchor on one. Match the proposal's Register title (`filing of … petition`) to set them apart. A count of lifecycles counts docketed proceedings, not rulemakings: FNA's three open lifecycles on that snapshot are one RIN, 0584-AF22, in dockets FNA-2026-0034, -0166 and -0201; count distinct `proceedings.rin` for rulemakings.

classes.label: Rulemaking lifecycle events
classes.summary: One dated stage event per document in a docketed proceeding. A uniquely resolved Federal Register number supplies its document type and date; otherwise the Regulations.gov type and upload day apply. Only Rule/Proposed Rule types create those stages: Notice entries and withdrawn postings do not. A dated Unified Agenda withdrawal can add a withdrawal event. Main document identity and date-source fields preserve those distinctions.
classes.coverage: Derived, and bounded by its inputs: the stage events of every docketed proceeding, one per document, less those undated or dated after the run's day.

classes.label: Time to final rule by agency
classes.summary: Estimated days to a final rule by agency and stratum, using Aalen–Johansen cumulative incidence with withdrawal as a competing outcome and 95% intervals. Cells pool all proposal years; fewer than 30 rules suppress estimates. NULL quartiles mean the estimate never reaches that probability. Routine families exist only for FAA, EPA and USCG. Each docketed proceeding counts separately, including proposals naming several dockets. Cohort estimates require filtering and recomputing the underlying lifecycles.
classes.coverage: Derived from `rulemaking_lifecycles` with a survival outcome, every proposal year together (no cohort window), per `agency_code` as the proceeding states it (no department roll-up: HHS, CMS and FDA are separate cells). A cell covering fewer than 30 rules is suppressed.
classes.data_quality: On 2026-09-27 every unsuppressed estimate equalled R's multi-state `survfit`.

classes.label: Federal entity registry
classes.summary: One row per active SAM.gov registration, ingested from the Entity Management API v4 bulk extract (`/entities?format=json`) by `build_sam_entities`. The authoritative federal entity registry, the directory of organizations registered to do business with or receive assistance from the U.S. government. Its UEI is the identity `usaspending_recipients.uei` joins on. Comments carry no UEI, so a commenting organization reaches this table only by a name match on `legal_business_name` or `dba_name`, which is not an identity. Filtered to public active registrations (`registrationStatus=A`); list-level fields only.
classes.coverage: Window, complete for the years read. Every public active registration SAM.gov dated 1996 through 2026 and the two older ones (1949, 1968), one bulk extract per registrationDate year; each year matched its active count when read, less its credited renewals (see data_quality), and the output ledger records the counts. Scheduled runs re-read the current year every other day and cycle through the older years between, and each year read replaces that year's rows.
classes.data_quality: A row is a registration, keyed by `uei` and `entity_eft_indicator`: one entity registers once per EFT indicator (187 of the 147,038 UEIs in the 2026 extract carry more than one), so `uei` alone is not unique. SAM keeps a renewed registration's prior record Active until its expiry is processed, and counts both; the table keeps the newer, and the reader credits the other toward the file's declared count (one each in 2007, 2008, 2011, 2013, 2019 and 2020 and two in 2026, each journaled). A file with fewer registrations than it declares, less those credits, is refused. A year read retires the registrations it no longer holds (80 expired from 2002 and 2003 and 11 from 2026 on 2026-09-26), journaled as `rows-retired` so qualification reconciles every removal. A stalled extract is abandoned and triggered afresh, each abandonment journaled.

classes.label: Lobbying disclosure filings
classes.summary: One row per federal lobbying-disclosure filing, ingested from the U.S. Senate Lobbying Disclosure Act (LDA) REST API (`lda.gov`, formerly `lda.senate.gov`) by `build_lobbying_filings`. Registrants file quarterly reports naming the clients they lobby for, the money involved, the issues raised, and the government entities (agencies/chambers) lobbied — so this table links the comment campaigns in `comments`/`dockets` to the same organizations' *direct* agency lobbying. Primary / dedup key is `filing_uuid`.
classes.coverage: True range: every filing of each filing year held, read whole from the LDA API, from the earliest filing year the backfill has reached to date; earlier years are added one year per dispatched run (owner decision 47). Query min(filing_year) for the current start.

classes.label: Lobbying activities
classes.summary: One row per lobbying activity an LDA filing reports: the issue area, the registrant's description of what was lobbied, foreign-entity interests, and the government entities contacted for that activity. Keyed `(filing_uuid, activity_index)`, the position in the filing's own list, which is stable because LDA never edits a filing (an amendment is a new filing). Joins to `lobbying_filings` on `filing_uuid`.
classes.coverage: True range, the same filings as `lobbying_filings`: one row per lobbying activity a filing reports. A filing that lists no activity has no rows here.

classes.label: Lobbyists named on lobbying activities
classes.summary: One row per lobbyist an LDA filing names on one of its activities, with the lobbyist's LDA id and name parts, any covered official position they held, and whether the filing lists them as new. Keyed `(filing_uuid, activity_index, lobbyist_index)`, positions in the filing's own lists. Joins to `lobbying_activities` on `(filing_uuid, activity_index)` and to `lobbying_filings` on `filing_uuid`.
classes.coverage: True range, the same filings as `lobbying_filings`: one row per lobbyist named on each activity. An activity that names no lobbyist has no rows here.

classes.label: Political committees
classes.summary: One row per observed Federal Election Commission committee. The current reader acquires from the unfiltered OpenFEC `/v1/committees/` endpoint through SpicyDocs; the delivered seed's selected scope is stated above. SpicyRegs preserves the registry's fields, merges complete fresh traversals with prior observations by committee_id, and lets a fresh whole row replace its prior row. Raw page captures and acquisition manifests remain in FEC_CAPTURE_DIR. This identity/reference table can join other records carrying an FEC committee identifier. The company, union or association behind a PAC (FEC's connected organization) is not a column here: join `fec_committee_history` on committee_id and read `connected_organization_name`, one value per two-year cycle as that cycle's committee master states it (take the latest cycle for the current sponsor). first_file_date and last_file_date are dates, cycles and candidate_ids are native lists, and the other columns are text.
classes.coverage: Not a range. The OpenFEC committee registry: the whole registry is walked every Sunday (decision 53) and committees that filed in the last week are read daily; rows only an earlier walk saw are kept. first_file_date and last_file_date describe filing activity, not acquisition.

Inspect each collection's retained selection and source coordinates before combining observations. classes.data_quality: Names never become IDs. Identifier shape checks do not verify the named entity or prove the reference resolves. classes.label: Commenter organizations matched to committees
classes.summary: One row per (commenter organization name, FEC committee) name match, derived by `build_org_committee_links`. Materializes the organization-name bridge between the regulations.gov corpus and `fec_committees` — the join the data model always described but left to each query author, so every consumer normalized names differently. `organization` is the raw string as filed, joining straight back to `comments.organization`; `committee_id` joins to `fec_committees`. Coverage is inherently small: `comments.organization` is stated on a small share of comments (`count(organization)` over `comments` is the measure) and on none at some agencies (FDA, EPA), and most commenting organizations do not run a federal PAC, so most organization names matching no committee is the expected outcome rather than a matcher to tune harder. Matching runs in three tiers (`exact`, `core`, `prefix`) and every row carries `match_method`, `confidence`, and `committee_match_count` so consumers pick their own precision bar instead of trusting an opaque score. A high `committee_match_count` can reflect multiple committees sharing a name prefix; inspect the source evidence before treating those matches as an affiliation network. The comment counts and dates on a row cover every agency and year the comments table holds and repeat on each committee row of the same organization string.
classes.coverage: Derived, and bounded by a small input. Name matches between commenter organizations and FEC committees, reachable only for the small share of comments that carry an `organization` value at all, so absence of a link is not evidence that a commenter has none. A candidate's committee or a leadership PAC is never linked.
classes.data_quality: These are heuristic name matches, not source-reported affiliations. `confidence` grades the matching rule alone, not a measured probability: it does not look at whether the committee still files or at the sponsor FEC states. Links to a candidate's committee (FEC committee type `H`, `S` or `P`) or a member's leadership PAC (designation `D`) are left out, because such a committee is never an organization's own (25 of 25 sampled were false, 2026-10-03). `connected_organization_name` and `sponsor_name_match` add FEC's own statement of each committee's sponsor beside the grade: in a seeded sample of 45 `high` links (2026-10-03, judged from FEC's committee records), 15 of 15 that agree, 13 of 15 that differ and 12 of 15 with no stated sponsor were the commenting organization's own committee or filing. Whether a committee has terminated is in `fec_committees`, one join away on `committee_id`: `filing_frequency` `T` (terminated) or `A` (administratively terminated), and `last_file_date`. A link to a terminated committee can still be right, for a comment filed while the committee was active.

classes.label: Government Accountability Office reports
classes.summary: One GAO report or testimony, keyed by product ID. GovInfo, GAO listings/RSS, retained package data and explicit repairs supply records. The table retains earlier observations and fills missing cells; source routes have different periods and metadata. Native `/3` rows expose product URL and source route; earlier schemas retain them in receipts. Major-rule letters provide separate source-stated agency, date and RIN fields, with reading evidence in receipts.
classes.coverage: True range on GovInfo's closed archive (1989-11-15–2008-09-18), combined with bounded GAO listings, recent RSS reads, retained package data and explicit repairs. Completed GAO listing scopes extend from 2009; major-rule listings reach April 1996. Recent RSS reads began 2026-09-22 and first reached 2026-09-15; the upstream copy covers 2026-07-13–2026-09-14. The retained R package reaches 1922 but adds only otherwise unheld reports. Intermediate periods remain incomplete where listing walks or repairs have not filled them. Numbered legal decisions belong to `gao_decisions`. Missing enrichment is not proof of an absent report.
classes.data_quality: GovInfo metadata is read in batches; a missing report number can mean unread or unavailable MODS. Major-rule letter fields use product-page/PDF captures from 2026-10-04; later products remain blank until read. Package-supplied requester, recommendation, matters, page-count and subject fields can be missing on later reports. Product-page enrichment is implemented but disabled; its absence does not remove report records. GAO listing issue dates and Month in Review release dates differ. The retained R package (CetiAlphaFive/gao, GPL-3.0-or-later, commit 6f61230) supplements other sources and excludes legal decisions. Unnumbered products are excluded. A retained source route does not certify complete coverage of its archive.

classes.label: Congressional Research Service reports
classes.summary: One Congressional Research Service report from the Congress.gov API list, keyed by `report_id`. Whole or pooled list walks validate the declared population; updates follow source `update_date`. This is list metadata only: report details and bodies are not fetched. `published_date` dates the current version, not first publication. The source API locator is retained in receipts.
classes.coverage: True range: reports whose current version is dated from 1993-10-22 on (`published_date` is the current version's date, not first issue).

classes.label: Court dockets of APA suits against agencies
classes.summary: One CourtListener docket object selected as nature-of-suit 899, an Administrative Procedure Act case. Search API and bulk sources cover mainly district courts; direct appellate challenges are largely absent. Agency names in case/party text identify candidates, not confirmed regulatory links. `cl_docket_id` identifies a docket object, not necessarily a unique case; use `court_docket_groups` to inspect related objects and retain reused-number ambiguity.
classes.coverage: True range with a density caveat: dockets filed from 1992 on, but only the nature-of-suit 899 (Administrative Procedure Act) selection, not the full docket record. Party names of dockets from the bulk edition are read a bounded slice per run; until read, parties is NULL. Recall against the publisher's nature-of-suit coding is unmeasured.

classes.label: Court docket same-case groups
classes.summary: One docket object's membership in an inferred same-case group. Shared court/number alone is insufficient: matching captions, or a same-day contained caption, qualify the group. `confidence_tier` separates per-defendant dockets from duplicate records. The representative is a selected display row, not a publisher-designated main case. Grouping is limited to the stated CourtListener bulk edition; reused numbers and later objects may remain ungrouped.
classes.coverage: Not a range. A derived mapping over the published `court_dockets` selection, computed from CourtListener's bulk docket edition named in `edition`. The grouping evaluates every published row whose court and docket number hold two or more published rows and which that edition holds. Such a row has no group when the rows under its number show no sign of one case (different captions: a court reusing a number) or none has a numeric PACER case id; a row published after the edition has no group until the grouping is recomputed.

classes.label: Court decisions and their opinion groups
classes.summary: Decision metadata from CourtListener opinion-clusters bulk data and opinion-search catch-up. cluster_id joins court_opinions.cluster_id (and through it the citation map and parentheticals); cl_docket_id joins court_dockets.cl_docket_id only where both tables hold the same publisher docket object: an appellate decision can name a scraper-created docket while court_dockets holds the RECAP one, so match on the docket number when the id does not join. Court identity comes from a bulk docket map or a search result; jurisdiction classification uses CourtListener's court reference data. This table does not hold individual opinion bodies.
classes.coverage: Not a range. The complete 2026-06-30 CourtListener opinion-clusters export, every mapped source field checked against the original export; the court fields agree with the same-edition docket map and court reference data. A search catch-up adds every cluster whose id is above the export's highest, whatever its filing date; a correction to an exported cluster arrives with the next export. Opinion bodies and broader historical coverage are separate. Per-court gaps are the publisher's: cadc has no unpublished cluster between 2001-04 and 2020-07. See docs/research/fork-output-ledger-2026-09-21.md and receipt join-gaps-2026-09-26/i/.
classes.data_quality:
Bulk and search records expose different fields. ingest_source identifies the selected row's route; unavailable metadata may be NULL or blank. A search row never replaces a bulk row of the same export, whose ids it lies above, and a later export's bulk row replaces it. Opinion search does not index RECAP trial-court clusters, so one created after the export arrives only with the next export. Missing court scope is unknown, not proof of a non-federal court. court_dockets is a narrower selection, so unmatched docket IDs are expected. Names, judge strings and citations do not establish cross-source identity.
One decision can be several clusters. On the 2026-06-30 export (measured 2026-10-03), 131 of the 140 Supreme Court decisions reported in 600-606 U.S., grouped by `cl_docket_id` and U.S. citation, have two to five clusters, none with an `scdb_id`. That grouping is a heuristic: it cannot see a decision with no reporter citation yet.

classes.label: Court reporter citations
classes.summary: Every reporter citation CourtListener records for a decision, such as "410 U.S. 113", "93 S. Ct. 705" or a WestLaw or neutral cite. Join cluster_id to court_opinion_clusters.cluster_id to reach the decision; a U.S. Reports citation found in a document (SpicyDocs' us_reports_cite rule) resolves through the rows with reporter 'U.S.', to every cluster carrying it (often two for a recent Supreme Court decision). Rebuilt whole from each quarterly export. All columns are VARCHAR, copied as the publisher wrote them.
classes.coverage: Not a range. The complete 2026-06-30 CourtListener citations export, copied field for field: every (cluster_id, volume, reporter, page) unique as the publisher's schema requires. The publisher cut this export hours after the cluster export, so a few citations name a cluster court_opinion_clusters lacks (63 on 2026-09-26, 43 of them added by the clusters' catch-up; receipt join-gaps-2026-09-26/i/).
classes.data_quality: Citations are the publisher's, not re-derived from opinion text; a decision missing a citation here may still carry one in print. Reporter strings are the publisher's abbreviations and are not normalized. page is text because some reporters page with letters or asterisks. A new export is refused until the published court_opinion_clusters reaches every cluster id it names; a cluster the publisher merged away after the export still dangles. The 2026-06-30 export holds no S. Ct. citation in volumes 143 and 144 (measured 2026-10-03).

classes.label: Court opinion citation map
classes.summary: Which court opinion cites which, and how often, as CourtListener's citator resolved it. Both ids are opinion ids, not decision ids: join each to court_opinions.opinion_id, then court_opinions.cluster_id to court_opinion_clusters, to ask what cites a decision or which decisions are cited most. Rebuilt whole from each quarterly export.
classes.coverage: Not a range. The complete 2026-06-30 CourtListener citation-map export: citing/cited opinion pairs, each unique as the publisher's schema requires, with no NULL depth. Only the publisher's surrogate row id is dropped. Citing and cited ids resolve through court_opinions of the same edition except a small residue (see data_quality).
classes.data_quality: On 2026-09-22 all but 3,758 citing ids and one cited id resolved through court_opinions of the same edition. The edges are the publisher's automated citation resolution, not a reviewed citator: citations it could not resolve are absent, and depth counts mentions, not treatment (followed, distinguished or overruled are not recorded). Several opinions of one decision each carry their own edges, and so do several clusters of one decision (see court_opinion_clusters.cluster_id): count decisions, not rows or clusters, by `scdb_id` where it is set, else by the heuristic `cl_docket_id` plus reporter citation, and query every cluster of a cited decision. Edges reach a recent decision late: Loper Bright (decided 2024-06-28) has one citing decision filed in 2024 against 151 for Chevron over the same months, and none of its citing clusters was created before 2025-01-13 (measured 2026-10-03 on the 2026-06-30 export); the publisher does not say why.

classes.label: Court opinion parentheticals
classes.summary: Short summaries of a decision written by the courts that later cite it, the text in parentheses after a citation, such as "(holding that an agency must explain a change in position)". described_opinion_id is the opinion summarized and describing_opinion_id the one that wrote it; join either to court_opinions.opinion_id to reach its decision. score is the publisher's estimate of how descriptive the text is. Rebuilt whole from each quarterly export.
classes.coverage: Not a range. The complete 2026-06-30 CourtListener parentheticals export, none with empty text; some have no group. Described and describing opinion ids resolve through court_opinions of the same edition except a small residue (see data_quality).
classes.data_quality: On 2026-09-22 every described opinion id and all but 618 describing ids resolved through court_opinions of the same edition. The text is the citing court's own words, extracted automatically by the publisher, so it can describe a holding, a fact or a procedural point, and score is a model estimate, not a review. Several parentheticals can summarize the same point; group_id links those the publisher grouped. The groups themselves are not available: the publisher's schema declares search_parentheticalgroup (schema-2026-06-30.sql), but no bulk listing exports it (0 of 1,076 keys on 2026-09-22), so group_id has no lookup table here.

classes.label: Court opinions (index, no text)
classes.summary: Every CourtListener opinion's decision, type and author, without its text. It is what connects court_citation_map and court_parentheticals, which name opinions, to court_opinion_clusters, which holds CourtListener's decision records (one decision can have several): join opinion_id from either, then cluster_id to court_opinion_clusters.cluster_id. local_path and download_url locate the original document. Rebuilt whole from each quarterly export, locally rather than on a schedule, because the source export is 54.6 GB.
classes.coverage: Not a range. The complete 2026-06-30 CourtListener opinions export without its eight text fields: every opinion_id unique and every cluster_id set. All but 21 name a decision in court_opinion_clusters; those 21 are RECAP trial-court opinions created between the two exports, which opinion search does not index, and resolve with the next export (receipt join-gaps-2026-09-26/i/). Opinion text is not included: the fork links out to CourtListener instead.
classes.data_quality: Author strings are the publisher's text and are not resolved to people; author_id is set only where the publisher linked a judge. opinion_type is the publisher's code, such as 010combined or 040dissent.

classes.label: Selected court opinion PDF text
classes.summary: Recorded PDF text for selected CourtListener opinions. Failed fingerprint or extraction checks supply no text. Following an opinion requires published capture and parent-publication evidence, plus its opinion ID, cluster ID, fingerprint and source URL together. A shared digest alone does not identify the parent.
classes.coverage: Sampled. Selected publisher PDFs acquired in one cohort. Each exact body matches its held CourtListener SHA-1 and has its own SHA-256 and extraction outcome. This is derived PDF text, separate from CourtListener native text fields and from the complete opinion index. Receipt: spicy-regs-court-cohort-20260927/bodies-receipt.json.

classes.label: Member vote terms
classes.summary: The term each member vote counts toward (delivery decision 2). A vote on `vote_day` counts toward the term with `term_start <= vote_day < term_end`, so the day one Congress ends and the next begins belongs to the new term. Only where that finds none is an inclusive end accepted, and only if exactly one term qualifies. The term type follows the chamber (`rep`, `sen`); a term with no end date never matches. Built by `build_member_vote_terms` from `member_votes`, whose `bioguide_id` the votes rollup resolves for a Senate row (from its LIS id) and for a House row of 1990-2002 (from its printed label), and `member_terms`. Join to `member_votes` on (`vote_id`, `member_key`) and to `member_terms` on (`bioguide_id`, `term_index`).
classes.coverage: Derived, and bounded by its inputs: one row for every `member_votes` row, matched to the member's term on the vote date.
classes.data_quality: On 2026-09-23 all but 18 votes matched a half-open term: 15 matched only an inclusive end date and 3 matched no term, exactly as an independent replay found (fork-execution-2026-09-21/votes-qualification/complete-member-join-replay.json).

classes.coverage: Derived exact identity links over pinned scorecard and congressional tables. Historical context constrains member matches; unresolved and ambiguous identities remain visible. No fuzzy matching or score conversion is applied.

classes.coverage: Derived exact identity links over pinned scorecard and congressional tables. Historical context constrains member matches; unresolved and ambiguous identities remain visible. No fuzzy matching or score conversion is applied.

The selected Common Cause 2022 House DISCLOSE item compares dated cosponsorship with its explicit source cutoff. Other items and score reproduction are deferred. The public recipient API ranks trailing-12-month federal awards: daily reads refresh the top 10,000 and weekly walks select the positive-amount tail. Rows outside a selection retain prior amounts. classes.coverage: Not a range. Weekly walks select recipients with positive trailing-12-month awards; daily reads refresh the top of the ranking. Recipients outside a run's selection keep earlier amounts, so reporting periods can differ. Observation time and source digest belong to receipts when retained; older evidence may lack them. Absence does not prove the recipient has no federal awards.

classes.label: Medicare Part D drug spending
classes.summary: Source-reported drug and manufacturer spending for one explicitly selected benefit year, with separate Overall rows and literal source evidence.
classes.coverage: Sampled by design; source coverage is not measured by this schema. The date records this design statement, not a source measurement. The mapper requires one complete admitted Part D release and selects its benefit year. Original rows retain other supplied years. This does not establish current prices, net spending, all Medicare coverage or all historical releases. Local and public qualification are separate.

classes.label: Medicaid drug spending
classes.summary: Source-reported drug and manufacturer spending for one explicitly selected benefit year, with separate Overall rows and literal source evidence.
classes.coverage: Sampled by design; source coverage is not measured by this schema. The date records this design statement, not a source measurement. The mapper requires one complete admitted Medicaid release and selects its benefit year. Original rows retain other supplied years. This does not establish current prices, net spending, all Medicaid services or beneficiaries or all historical releases. CMS excludes drugs with fewer than 11 claims in the latest year and redacts earlier-year cells below that threshold. A missing drug is not evidence of zero spending. Actual qualification is recorded by the selected generation and retained source evidence.

Excludes Medicare Advantage and other claims excluded by the CMS methodology. Actual qualification is recorded by the selected generation and retained source evidence.

classes.coverage: Not a range. Every entity in each explicitly admitted selected export is retained. Selected SDN and consolidated exports need not share an update time. classes.label: Treasury daily debt balances
classes.summary: Treasury Debt to the Penny stock balances for explicitly selected dates, retaining exact dollars and source release identity.
classes.coverage: Sampled: explicitly selected Debt to the Penny observation dates for United States federal debt. A balance is a stock, not borrowing during the day or a budget deficit. Missing requested dates refuse rather than substituting the latest observation.

classes.label: Treasury monthly and fiscal-year budget actuals
classes.summary: Monthly Treasury Statement Table 1 receipts, outlays and deficit, with separate report and economic periods and preserved revisions.
classes.coverage: Sampled: complete declared Table 1 report issues. Supported shape requires current fiscal-year months from October through the report month, complete prior fiscal years, and a separate fiscal-year-to-date row per parent. Other layouts refuse. Table 2 cells are typed in treasury_statement_classification_cells; other statement tables are not typed here.

classes.label: Treasury budget results and financing by classification
classes.summary: Monthly Treasury Statement Table 2 cells, one per native line and measure, with literal amounts, per-field units and explicit No Transactions, zero and null markers.
classes.coverage: Sampled: explicitly selected MTS issues (2015-03-31, 2025-09-30, 2025-10-31, 2026-03-31 and 2026-09-30 qualified locally). Every issue must carry the 15-line native layout; each 0.00 estimate needs a page-5 review entry in treasury_units.json, and the on/off, receipts-outlays, financing and means-of-financing identities plus the Table 1 month, FYTD and prior-FYTD values refuse on mismatch. Identities skip cells without a number, so editions whose estimates print No Transactions verify fewer estimate identities. One publisher inconsistency ships under a digest-pinned exception: in 2025-09-30 the prior-FYTD means of financing (lines 13-15) exceed financing (line 11), as printed on page 5; the values are unchanged and the gap is pinned in treasury_units.json. Estimates are stated in $ millions; amount_usd scales them to dollars without adding precision.

classes.label: ACS county population and household income
classes.summary: One row per selected county and measure in an American Community Survey five-year vintage, with estimates, margins of error and exact source cells.
classes.coverage: Sampled by design only; source coverage has not been measured. Comparisons describe estimates, not statistically significant differences or individual households.

classes.label: FCC proceedings
classes.summary: One FCC ECFS docket, keyed by its name, with native proceeding ID retained separately. Full validated creation-date walks refresh its status. Where ECFS has several documents for a name, selection prefers the original docket and then the latest edited record. Unnamed or undated records are excluded. ECFS is separate from Regulations.gov and requires an api.data.gov key. Titles are not complete topic descriptions; open dockets may have placeholder close dates.
classes.coverage: True range: every proceeding ECFS dates, created from 1991 on, re-read whole each run so later closings and status changes are current. A proceeding with no created date is left out, because the API's date-range queries cannot reach it.

classes.label: FCC filings
classes.summary: One FCC ECFS submission, including comments, replies, ex-parte notices and letters, keyed by `id_submission`. The public API requires an api.data.gov key. Incremental received-date windows are validated by whole or pooled list walks. A first run defaults to the trailing 30 days; earlier history requires an explicit date or proceeding scope.
classes.coverage: Window. FCC ECFS filings received from 2026-08-24 onward, extended daily; earlier filings appear only in explicitly backfilled proceedings. Daily runs reread the trailing seven received-date days, so later dissemination can be missed. The newest day is partial. Proceedings reflect the last read and may retain a placeholder later reassigned by ECFS. PDF text extraction covers selected documents only; a held proceeding's count is not its ECFS total.

The current native schema includes the publisher's web address in `source_url` and the location within it in `source_path`; earlier schemas keep them in receipts; see etl_receipts.

classes.summary: One publisher-defined edition, with a series_id for continuity; a live series is not itself an edition. Values and preferred actions belong to the named publisher. Source evidence defaults to metadata and hashes; original bodies are retained publicly only under an established redistribution policy. The current native schema includes the publisher's web address in `source_url` and the location within it in `source_path`; earlier schemas keep them in receipts; see etl_receipts.
classes.coverage: Sampled publisher editions selected by the scorecard source registry. Complete edition reads replace that edition; failed or incomplete reads preserve prior observations. Coverage varies by publisher and historical source format.

classes.summary: One complete accepted edition capture and parse; unsuccessful attempts remain in the run journal. Values and preferred actions belong to the named publisher. Source evidence defaults to metadata and hashes; original bodies are retained publicly only under an established redistribution policy.
classes.coverage: Sampled publisher editions selected by the scorecard source registry. Complete edition reads replace that edition; failed or incomplete reads preserve prior observations. Coverage varies by publisher and historical source format.

classes.label: Scorecard methodologies
classes.summary: One source-stated rule set in an edition, scoped to chamber and cohort as stated. Values and preferred actions belong to the named publisher. On the measured cold-start run of the 119th (receipt `d1-measured-run-2026-09-19/`) the family reported **21,466** such refusals against 6,301 published rows — one per printing whose body the 600-per-run fetch cap did not reach, plus those offered only as PDF. The refusal count is therefore a measure of how far the cap is from the corpus, not of anything wrong with the printings; it falls as successive runs spend the cap on ground earlier ones did not reach. A section is keyed on its `seq` within the printing since spicy-docs 0.35.0; the older key (`match_path`, `body_index`) repeats inside a printing.

classes.label: Bill version comparisons
classes.summary: One row per compared pair of consecutive printings of one bill. `engine_name`, `engine_version` and `engine_revision` record which diff engine produced the row.

classes.data_quality: A consecutive pair that cannot be diffed — because one or both sides has no parsed tree — is a counted refusal named by table, never a row. Measured on the cold-start run of the 119th (receipt `d1-measured-run-2026-09-19/`): **3,185** refusals against 128 published comparisons, which is what a 600-printing cap over 22,064 printings implies, since a pair needs both of its sides fetched in the same run. A pair runs from a printing to its neighbour in spicy-docs' `printing_order`: publisher date, then a dateless enrolled printing by its stage (`pair_rule` `consecutive_by_date_then_stage`). A pair's neighbour can be a procedural printing (a four-section Senate engrossed amendment between the calendar printing and the enrolled bill), which the summary route refuses but this table compares, so the pair reads as nearly everything removed and then everything added. In `section_diff_items`, `financial_amounts_changed` is true on every added or removed row that carries a figure, by construction; only a modified row says a figure changed in place. Floor-amendment annotations (`(increased by $X)`) are left out of `financial_*_amounts_json` though they change the text; `financial_has_amendment_annotations` marks them. Enrolled printings carry new element ids at the publisher, so `element_id` does not join into `enr`.

classes.label: Amendments
classes.summary: One row per amendment, from the Congress.gov amendment list and detail routes. Keyed on the amendment's own identity, not the bill it amends, because an amendment can amend another amendment; `amended_bill_id` and `amended_amendment_id` are foreign keys. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.
classes.coverage: Window: the 119th Congress, each amendment with its detail record (the output ledger records its qualification). Scheduled runs walk an `updateDate` window from the table's watermark, at most ninety days, and fetch detail for each amendment in it.
classes.data_quality: The publisher's `updateDate desc` order repeats and skips amendments across page boundaries when stamps tie, so one walk can serve the declared count while missing some amendments. The builder repeats whole walks, alternating order and page size, and settles on the first of two things: a clean walk (no amendment repeated, its distinct count the declared count), which stands alone, or the walks since the count last changed pooled to exactly the declared count. A pool larger than the count is never published, but a later clean walk can still settle; a query unsettled after its walks refuses the run, as does a record without an `updateDate`. Sponsor, chamber, submitted date and the amended bill or amendment come from each amendment's detail record; the list route carries none of them. 89 House amendments name the Rules Committee as sponsor and have no member sponsor to record. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.

classes.label: Appropriations press releases
classes.summary: One row per item in one appropriations committee press-release feed capture. `bill_id` is an inferred candidate when a pattern matches a published bill identifier in the title or description.
classes.coverage: Window. Releases from the House and Senate Appropriations committees' feeds as captured since September 19, 2026, including items that later rotated out of a feed; bill links are inferred from release text. Not all committees, earlier history or release-page bodies. See `press-release-qualification/` and `press-link-repair/` in the fork execution receipts.
classes.data_quality: The bill linkage is a pattern match over the release's own words, not a publisher statement. An earlier local run falsely matched `s 2027` inside a reference to the President's 2027 budget to Senate bill 2027. The corrected matcher rejects possessive suffixes while preserving quoted bill citations; wider matching quality remains unmeasured. `matched_field` and `matched_text` carry what was matched and where: a false positive is readable from the row rather than only by re-running the matcher. One pattern is compiled per published bill in the Congresses in scope, bounded on both sides and built from the bill's own type, so a bare number matches nothing. Three states are distinct and must not be read as one: a `bill_id` with `match_rule = bill_number_in_title` or `bill_number_in_excerpt` is a match; `match_rule = unmatched` with a NULL `bill_id` means the matcher ran and found no pattern match; an all-NULL `match_rule` means no matching pass ran at all, because no `congress_bills` table was published when the rollup ran, or none was published for that release's Congress, or the release states no readable `pub_date` to scope by. The Senate feed carries no item description, so a Senate release can only ever match on its title. One consequence worth knowing before relying on these four columns: a run that cannot read `congress_bills` republishes the whole live window with NULL match columns, because this table merges row-wise and a fresh row wins whole. The next run that can read it re-derives them for every release still in the feed, so the gap normally lasts one cycle — but a release that rotates off the feed during that cycle keeps the NULL permanently. The other publisher columns are unaffected; only these four degrade.

classes.label: House and Senate roll-call votes
classes.summary: One row per roll call: the publisher's own tally, and the bill it refers to. The four tally columns are the publisher's own counts, NULL on a candidate election (a Speaker vote), whose choices `tallies` keeps under their own labels. A Senate count element the file leaves empty or omits (`<present/>`, `<absent/>`) is read as 0, which is what the Senate means by it (119-senate-1-15: 50 yea, 50 nay, 0 present, 0 absent).
classes.coverage: Sampled, and accumulating. Independent Senate LIS session lists and House Clerk roll files supply votes under per-run caps. The scheduled scope is the current Congress; older Congresses require backfill. Clerk history begins in 1990, in the 101st Congress; bill-derived vote references begin in the 108th. A failed chamber listing preserves its prior rows, so chambers can lag separately. Recent votes may be reread for corrections. Bill references alone do not prove a complete session index. `vote_date` retains publisher spelling and is not a sortable date bound.
classes.data_quality: Two statements link a roll call to a bill, and `match_rule` names the one that did. `bill_action_recorded_vote`: a `recordedVotes` entry on the bill's own action, read from `bill_vote_references`. `vote_file_legislation`: the vote file's own statement of its measure, the Clerk's `legis_num` or the Senate's document, with the file's own URL as `match_url`; on a Senate amendment vote that document is `S.Amdt.`, not a bill, so such a roll call links to a bill only where the rollup resolved one through the bill's own recorded-vote action (`count(bill_id)` over amendment votes is the measure). The bill's action wins; where two bills' actions record one roll call, the one the file names wins (the Senate passing a House bill after its Senate twin); with no recorded reference the file links alone. A procedural question, a nomination, a treaty or two different bills link nothing. Measured on the 108th and 119th (receipt `votes-backfill-2026-09-26/file-links/`), the files add 881 links and agree with the recorded reference on 1,803 of the 1,809 roll calls both link; the six others are those Senate passages. `conflict_count` is per roll call, not per run: it counts the later references, the file's included, that named a different bill for *this* roll call, and they are kept rather than dropped. Before 2003 only the file's `legis_num` links: it links 6,614 of the 7,327 files of 1990-2002 to 2,842 bills, 26 of which have no `congress_bills` row yet. A held row is relinked from its own columns without a fetch; a House row published before `legis_num` or `clerk_body_element` existed is read again once to gain both, with `vote_desc`. A Senate row published before `vote_question_text`, `vote_title`, `majority_requirement` and `modify_date` existed is read again once in the same way and gains them and any tie-breaker: until then its NULL tie-breaker columns say nothing about whether the vote was tied. The scheduled run reads the sitting Congress's such rows; an earlier Congress's are read when its number is dispatched. Replayed over the retained files of the 108th-118th, that read fills the element on all 14,503 published House rows (3,742 `committee`) and `vote_desc` on 9,191, and changes no other column and no member row; it also publishes the five votes the House vacated before recording a position, which have zero tallies, `member_vote_count` 0 and no `member_votes` rows. The Clerk's 2003 Speaker election (108-1-2), whose candidate totals contradict its members' choices, still refuses. The contract's `house_vote_legislation` rule (Congress.gov's `house-vote` listing) is no longer produced and no published row carries it: it was retired with the api.data.gov key it needed (2026-09-26). Each run fills a NULL `vote_day` on every held (completely captured) roll call from its own `vote_date` before merging, so a row published before the column existed gains it without a re-fetch. An incomplete capture is not held: it is re-fetched first each run and takes its day from the file. A linkage-only row keeps NULL.

classes.label: Member vote positions
classes.summary: One row per member's position on one roll call. `position` keeps the publisher's own word (the Clerk spells both Aye/No and Yea/Nay) and `position_normalized` carries the fold, so a count and a quotation are both answerable. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.
classes.coverage: Sampled, and accumulating. One row per member per roll call in `roll_call_votes`, so it inherits that table's both-chambers scope, per-run cap and skip-what-is-already-held behavior exactly.
classes.data_quality:
House rows with `state` `XX` are the non-voting delegates and the Resident Commissioner, as the Clerk marks them. The Clerk marks them only on amendment votes and motions in committee, so leave them out when ranking voting Representatives. A member who died before a term began can appear as Not Voting on its opening quorum call, as the Clerk's file lists them. One `bioguide_id` can carry more than one spelling of `member_name`; group by `bioguide_id`. The Clerk's files of 1990-2002 (the 101st-107th Congresses) name no member by bioguide id: their rows key `name:` plus the Clerk's label (`name:Jones (NC)`), and that key identifies the row within its roll call, not a person, since at least 21 labels of those years name two different members. The `bioguide_id` on such a row is resolved at the votes merge, not stated by the Clerk (rule `house-name-crosswalk-v4`): it is the one member of that surname, state and party seated in the House in that Congress, per `members`, `member_terms` and `member_party_affiliations`, and only where the vote's day lies inside that member's term. A printed first name chooses among several members when it equals the crosswalk's, in full, in its first word or as an initial, or when it is the nickname the crosswalk's source states for the member (`Tom` for Thomas Davis), which is read once `members` publishes it. Where several still answer to the label, as a successor of the same surname does (the 105th's Capps and Bono, the 107th's Shuster), the row takes the one of them seated on the vote's day; and on a day that seats several, a label that prints no first name is the member left once those the same roll call lists under a first name are set aside (the 101st's `Smith (OR)` beside `Smith, Denny (OR)`). Anything else stays NULL, and `member_vote_terms` leaves that row `unresolved_member`. Applied to the table published 2026-10-04, the rule resolves 3,173,468 of its 3,175,523 such rows with `members` as published, and 3,175,521 with the source's nicknames: the 101st's two Smiths of Oregon and the 107th's `Davis, Tom` (2,053 rows) wait for that column. The two rows then left are one that prints the Speaker `D` (106-house-1-2) and one dated the day after its member died. Run over the rows of 2003 on with the Clerk's own ids hidden and the source's nicknames, the rule filled 6,567,134 of 6,567,152 and differed from the Clerk on two: 109-house-1-239 and -240, which state M000249 (Robert Matsui, who died before that Congress met) on the row of Doris Matsui (M001163), as Voteview records those two votes. Those rows keep the id the Clerk states. Receipt: fork-execution-2026-09-21/votes-person-crosswalk-2026-10-05/. Senate rows carry the bioguide id resolved from their LIS id through `members` at the votes merge; a Senate row still NULL has a LIS id that `members` does not hold, or holds twice (`unresolved_member`).
The Clerk lists the Speaker only on the roll calls the Speaker votes on; on the others the Speaker has no row at all, not a Not Voting row (Johnson, J000299, has no row on 54 of the 314 House roll calls of 2026, measured 2026-10-03), so an absence rate over roll calls does not apply to the Speaker. `party` is the label the publisher printed on that roll call, and a change of label starts on the roll call that first prints it: the Clerk prints Kiley (K000401) `R` through roll 95 (2026-03-18) and `I` from roll 96 (2026-03-19), while `member_party_affiliations` dates the change 2026-03-09. Use `party` for a split as the chamber recorded it, and `member_party_affiliations` for a party as of a date.
