classes.data_quality: Only the MODS PRIMARY bill fills bill_id. The CBO columns come from spicy-docs read_cbo_estimate on the same body already acquired. The cover recital gates publication of a letter: a CBO heading alone is not an estimate. report_states_estimate=false records an absent recital; NULL means the rule has not run. cbo_letter_count counts the letters located in the part, each a committee_report_cbo_letters row; a positive recital with a count of 0 is a declared estimate no letter was located for, distinct from an extracted letter. The five per-letter columns this table carried until committee_reports legislative-documents/2 (the first letter's span, digest, end rule and signatory) are on committee_report_cbo_letters, one row per letter (ss-uep5). estimate_heading stays here with a two-sided meaning: the part's first estimate heading where no located letter opens on it, NULL where one does (that letter's row carries it). It keeps all 115 headings of live generation 670476640e83 that open no letter, among them 110 undeclared reports' "Congressional Budget Office Cost Estimate" sections saying none was received; the other 29 live headings opened a letter and are on its row. recital_bill_id comes from the printed recital and is retained beside the MODS bill_id. bill_id is the part's own PRIMARY bill: a multi-part package's root states none, so each part of CRPT-119hrpt494 carries the H.R. 3495 its constituent record names, where its row read before parts were keyed has NULL; its separate recital_bill_id is a text interpretation. Every part a record states is read, all or none: a package whose parts cannot all be read is refused in committee_report_reads and keeps its prior rows. Parts, by decision 29 (`docs/research/fork-delivery-decisions-2026-09-22.md`): a report published in one part is one row whose part_id is its package id and whose part_number is NULL; a report published as parts is one row per part, part_id the part's granule id (CRPT-119hrpt455-pt2) and part_number 1 to N, except that a Part 1 the publisher left unsuffixed (CRPT-119hrpt494) has part_id equal to the package id and part_number 1. A package whose one part is spelled -pt1 (CRPT-119hrpt811; spicy-docs `docs/tables.md` names the others it measured) is (package-pt1, 1), the same shape as Part 1 of two, so a reader counts a package's rows to tell a lone part from Part 1 of several. title, date_issued and last_modified are the package's and repeat on every part row. A row published before part_id existed is kept as its package's one part (part_id the package id, part_number NULL) until the package is read again, which replaces its rows as a set; the committee_report_reads rule version re-reads every report once for this, which is what re-keys the CRPT-119hrpt811 row published 2026-09-24 as (CRPT-119hrpt811-pt1, 1).

classes.label: CBO letters in committee reports
classes.summary: One row per CBO cost-estimate letter reprinted in one committee report part, keyed `(package_id, part_id, letter_seq)`. The span indexes into the text the parent row's text_sha256 digests; letter_date is the letterhead's dateline.
classes.coverage: Sampled. Every CBO cost-estimate letter located in the report parts of committee_reports whose cover declares the estimate; an omnibus report reprints several (CRPT-105hrpt149 has 11). A declared part with no located letter has no row here and cbo_letter_count 0 on its committee_reports row.
classes.data_quality: (package_id, part_id) names the committee_reports row the letter was read from and letter_seq counts from zero in reading order within that part. A 1997-2011 letter's span runs from its heading or CBO letterhead through the enclosed estimate's "Estimate approved by ... Analysis." line; 118th-Congress letters end at the Director's attribution. letter_date is NULL where the letter prints no dateline, as every 118th-Congress letter does (its date is cbo_cost_estimates' publication date). Census 2026-10-31 over the 202 retained PDF and 199 committee-reports HTM bodies: 117 and 24 letters, 113 and 3 of them dated, 5 PDF letters a bare transmittal whose enclosure prints no approval line.

classes.label: Committee report heading and text blocks
classes.summary: One row per heading or unheaded text block in one part of a committee report, keyed `(package_id, part_id, seq)`. `heading` preserves the source title; agency identity fields remain unresolved. `pattern` records which header pattern fired, which is this table's provenance column.
classes.coverage: Sampled. Heading/text blocks of the reports in committee_reports. heading retains the source title while agency_label and agency_key remain unresolved NULLs. HTML bodies carry no page boundaries, so none are inferred.
classes.data_quality: part_id names the committee_reports row a block was parsed from, so (package_id, part_id) is its parent, and seq counts from zero within that part. By decision 29 (`docs/research/fork-delivery-decisions-2026-09-22.md`) part_id is the package id for a report published in one part and the part's granule id for a report published as parts, CRPT-119hrpt494's unsuffixed Part 1 aside; a package whose one part is spelled -pt1 (CRPT-119hrpt811; spicy-docs `docs/tables.md` names the others it measured) carries that spelling, so the parent's row count tells a lone part from Part 1 of several. A block published before part_id existed carries its package id there until its report is read again, which replaces every block of the package.

classes.label: Hearing transcripts
classes.summary: One row per captured GovInfo hearing transcript. bill_id is always NULL: a hearing can concern several bills, represented in hearing_bill_links.
classes.coverage: Sampled. Selected hearing packages from GovInfo, each with its native event identifiers checked: package and body metadata, not speaker turns or complete hearing history.
classes.data_quality: Cover bills come from the package's MODS and cost no extra requests. BODY mentions do not become hearing links. event_id is the meeting the Congress.gov hearing record names (its associatedMeeting), carried as the publisher pairs them. NULL means that record names no meeting, or was refused, and `committee_report_reads` says which (its `outcome`). It does not mean no meeting exists: a meeting can list the transcript's jacket in `committee_meetings.hearing_jackets` without the hearing record naming it. That jacket route is the publisher's many-to-many listing, not a declared join: on committee-meetings generation 31e62420… (2026-10-03) 1,021 meetings list two or more distinct jackets and 1,075 (congress, jacket) values sit on two or more meetings. The declared event_id join reads `complete` because every event_id names a meeting row; that does not check the pairing: CHRG-118hhrg63377 names meeting 116369, an Oversight and Investigations hearing the same day, while its MODS and docs.house.gov place it at 116330. body_completeness says what the read text states about itself: a publisher_placeholder body is the publisher's notice that the document is only in the PDF. When the package offers that PDF it is read instead (pdf_extracted, with text_derivation naming the extraction); when it offers none, the notice is published as it stands. NULL on rows not re-read since the column was added.

classes.label: Hearing-to-bill links
classes.summary: One row per package, bill and link source, shaped by spicy-docs.
classes.coverage: Sampled. Bill references that the selected hearing packages' MODS records state on their cover. It does not show bills named only in constituent records, agendas, bill actions or transcript text, and does not measure recall; agenda acquisition remains deferred.
classes.data_quality: mods_cover means held_on. The package measured confirmation on 19 of 20 cover pairs and 18 of 18 pairs where cover and agenda agreed. Agenda links mean noticed, not held_on: agenda-only pairs were confirmed 1 of 18, contradicted 1 and unverifiable 16. Recall is unmeasured. Only 2 of 20 sampled House hearings and 0 of 3 Senate hearings stated COVER bills; a missing row does not establish that a hearing concerned no bills. A successfully re-read cover replaces that hearing's prior links, including an empty result. Unread or refused bodies retain their prior links. held_date is the one date the hearing's MODS states. A compiled volume that states several dates has held_date NULL and every native date, in source order, in held_dates; the list does not establish that each bill was considered on each date. Before link rule d06e0bd80ca1 (2026-09-25) such a volume's links carried its first date (CHRG-117shrg56721 states eleven), and rows not re-read since keep held_dates NULL. committee_system_code is the first of its hearing's hearing_transcripts.committee_system_codes, set again every run, so a link and its hearing state one committee key.

classes.label: CBO cost-estimate publication index
classes.summary: One row per bill and CBO publication, using build_bill_family's own cbo_cost_estimates output and spicy-docs' feed builder, merged by `merge_cbo_cost_estimates`: where both routes state one bill and publication, the BILLSTATUS row stands. One publication can stand under two bills, and both rows publish.
classes.coverage: Sampled. CBO estimates linked to held bills from the 108th Congress onward, combining BILLSTATUS metadata and per-Congress CBO feeds. The 112th and 113th use the feed alone. A Congress's feed contributes only after a scoped run reads it. Items without a bill link stay in `cbo_feed_items`. Missing rows do not prove CBO never scored a bill; a weekly estimate may cover several bills. CBO document bodies are not acquired.
classes.data_quality: The bill's cbo_cost_estimates_outcome distinguishes an absent or empty element, an unexpected shape, and populated estimates. An empty index does not establish that CBO never scored the bill. Report citations are the bill's list, not proof that each publication is reprinted in each report; the report's recital gate is evaluated separately. A feed row carries its bill's own BILLSTATUS report citations, read by the same run or carried from the bill's published rows, and NULL where neither names them. A successfully evaluated bill replaces its prior BILLSTATUS rows, including when the list is absent or empty; an unexpected list shape retains prior rows until a successful read can establish the current relationships. A feed read replaces its Congress's prior feed rows, so an item CBO withdraws or re-files leaves, and a feed that cannot be read keeps them. `found_by` says how each row names its bill; the rows published before it take `billstatus` in a one-time backfill. `title_bill_id` is the bill the estimate's title leads with: where it differs from `bill_id` (7 of the 12,732 BILLSTATUS rows on 2026-09-29), `bill_id` is a numbering error as published and `title_bill_id` the bill scored. A title leading with a public law reads through the published `laws` table, which held the 119th Congress alone on 2026-09-29, so such a title of an earlier Congress leaves `title_bill_id` NULL and a blank feed item titled by an earlier law has no row (110th P.L. 110-50 and 112th P.L. 112-8). CBO's 119th-Congress feed, read 2026-10-03, holds 53 items that name no bill and have no row, 48 of them weekly suspension estimates. 23 of them are among the feed's 674 items dated 2026: 21 suspension estimates, 62413 (reconciliation recommendations of the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs committee) and 62643 (the Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027).

classes.label: CBO cost-estimate feed items
classes.summary: One row per CBO publication as its feed lists it: the Congress, the date as `cbo_cost_estimates.pub_date` spells it, the title, link and description, and the `Bill_Number` exactly as stated (empty where CBO names no bill). Joined to `cbo_cost_estimates` on `publication_id`, the items with no estimate row are the ones naming no bill: CBO's weekly estimates of the bills the House takes up under suspension of the rules, a committee's reconciliation recommendations, and estimates filed under no number.
classes.coverage: Sampled: every item of CBO's keyless per-Congress cost-estimate feed for each Congress a bill-family run has read the feed of, from the 108th on, whether or not the item names a bill. A run reads each scoped Congress's feed whole and its items replace that Congress's prior items; a feed it could not read keeps them. The scheduled run reads the sitting Congress's feed; earlier Congresses fill only by a bill-family dispatch scoped to them.
classes.data_quality: An item that names no bill is the publisher's statement, not an extraction miss; its bills are listed only in CBO's own document, which is not requested. Measured with the spicy-docs reader over the 108th-119th feeds on 2026-10-03: 15,156 items, every one a row; 361 have no estimate row (352 name no bill, 9 are refused), 53 of them in the 119th, 48 of those suspension notices.

classes.label: Government Accountability Office legal decisions
classes.summary: One GAO legal decision page, identified by its stated number and URL. A page can list several B-numbers, and one number can have several pages. Completed listing walks refresh named decisions; retained page captions can add the full number list and decision date. `outcome` classifies source decision-status text. Native `/3` rows expose `listing_page`; earlier schemas retain it in receipts.
classes.coverage: True range from 2009 on, within completed GAO Month in Review and Annual Index walks. Includes numbered legal decisions and Contract Appeals Board decisions; major-rule reports belong to `gao_reports`. Unnumbered entries are excluded. Year scopes can span several months. Missing rows alone cannot distinguish an unread scope from a completed listing with no decisions.
classes.data_quality:
`released_date` is when GAO released the decision, not when it decided it; `decided_date` is that day, from the Date line of the decision page's caption, so a count by one differs from a count by the other: over the 6,361 pages captured on 2026-10-03 whose caption read, the release came a median 7 days after the decision (1,294 the same day, 219 more than 90 days after; appropriations decisions a median 0), and 24 pages state a release before the decision, as GAO published them. `decided_date` is NULL, and `b_numbers` and `b_numbers_truncated` are the listing's, where no page was read: on 2026-10-03, 2 pages could not be captured, 247 print no caption (a letter, a report, a decision posted without its text) and 6 refuse for a number GAO mistyped on the page or in the listing; that run's journal names each refused page with its reason. `b_numbers_truncated` `true` is a list still cut, as B-412940's 22 listed numbers are (its page carries no decision text). Apply `html.unescape` when matching a `title`. `outcome` is NULL where GAO's listing states no status sentence for a decision, and where it states one spicy-docs' table leaves unmapped (a cost recommendation, an advisory or appropriations opinion and the like); each run's journal counts both.
GAO's own bid protest statistics, in its annual reports to Congress, are not a count of these rows: GAO counts docket numbers (B-numbers) as cases, not decision pages or procurements, per fiscal year, and takes its sustain rate over merit decisions (sustained plus denied). Here a row is one decision page, which can carry several B-numbers, dated by its release. The annual reports are rows of `gao_reports` (`GAO Bid Protest Annual Report to Congress for Fiscal Year …`) with title, date, link and at most a short abstract: their figures are not held. `decision_type` is GAO's label as its listing states it, not a check: GAO also labels a few reports `Bid Protest Decision` (B-423717, its response to section 885 of the FY2025 NDAA, and B-401197, a report to Congress on defense bid protests).

classes.label: Enacted laws
classes.summary: One row per enacted law the Congress.gov law list route states, with the Statutes at Large citation from the law's own PLAW USLM file where captured. Keyed on the law's Congress, type and number, not on the bill; `bill_id` is the foreign key to `congress_bills`, whose `statutes_at_large_cite` the host fills from this table at that table's merge.
classes.coverage: Sampled. Every law the Congress.gov law route lists for the scoped Congresses (the current one by default), walked whole each run; the PLAW USLM citation is added per law, newest first, under a per-run cap. A steady-state run is meant to ask only about laws whose list row moved or whose PLAW the bulk folder had not yet served.
classes.data_quality:
`statutes_at_large_cite` is set when `uslm_outcome` is `captured`; read every NULL through `uslm_outcome` and `uslm_reason`. `unavailable` (reason `source_unavailable`) is the publisher's own lag, a `404` from the exact PLAW locator: on 2026-09-19 the route listed 108 laws and the PLAW bulk folder held 104, the four newest (119-103, 119-104, 119-109, 119-110) absent; each is retried every run until the folder serves it.
`captured_partial` is a validated USLM file that states no Statutes at Large citation (reason `statutes_citation_not_stated`): the two private laws of the 119th (`PLAW-119pvtl1`, `PLAW-119pvtl2`), whose own `citableAs` values are kept in `uslm_citable_as`. Until reader rule `laws-uslm-v2` (2026-09-25) the contract refused those two files and their rows said `not_requested`, although both were requested and served. `captured_refused` keeps the digest of a `200` body the reader refused, either another law's file (`native_identity_refused`) or not native USLM at all, such as an HTML page (`native_shape_refused`), and none of its unvalidated fields. `request_failed` is an attempted read that established nothing, a transport failure included; it is never published as `unavailable`. `not_requested` means only that no request was made, which the per-run cap decides.
A validated row with parsed text is read again when its listing or metadata/text reader changes, or its matching section output is missing. A failed later attempt preserves its prior metadata and parsed sections. `law_text_outcome` distinguishes unread, parsed and refused text; an unavailable XML file does not mean the law has no provisions. Join `law_sections` on `law_id` for native sections. `law_body_remainder` retains main-body text outside those sections, including appropriation blocks; it is NULL unless parsed and may be an empty string on success. The section rows and remainder are printed law text, not consolidated current law. A publisher-refused Table III read is journaled `table3-bulk-refused` with reason `access-refused`, and the laws family publishes without the Table III rows that read would have added. `statutes_at_large_volume` follows the session that cleared the bill, not the year the law was approved: 119-69 and 119-71 to 119-73, approved in January 2026 on bills cleared in December 2025, are in volume 139, and 119-70 and 119-74 on are in volume 140. `statutes_at_large_last_page` comes with reader `laws-uslm-v3` (2026-10-03), so a row read under an earlier reader holds NULL there, which means not read, until the next laws run reads its PLAW again. `resolve_document_citations` resolves a Statutes citation to a page inside a law's range to that law and says the match is by range (`match_basis`); a law with no last page is matched by its first page only.

classes.label: Published law sections
classes.summary: One row per native section occurrence in a published law's main body. These are the law's own words, including amendment instructions, not a consolidated statement of current law. Section numbers and publisher IDs can repeat or be absent; (law_id, seq) identifies each occurrence and native_path locates it in the source XML. is_quoted marks sections inside quotedContent; parent_seq alone does not imply a quotation. Body excludes its own number and heading, print furniture, and nested sections' text; query the child rows as well. laws.law_body_remainder retains text outside all numbered sections, including appropriation blocks. Hierarchy retains the source context. Boolean and numeric observations use native types.
classes.coverage: Derived: source-native sections from identity-validated GovInfo public and private law XML acquired by the laws rollup. Join law_id to laws.law_id, then laws.bill_id to congress_bills.bill_id. A missing section row does not establish that the law has no text: check law_text_outcome and law_section_count in laws. Coverage follows successfully read XML, not all enacted laws. PDF-only sources are outside this reader.

classes.label: Law classifications by Congress
classes.summary: One row per line of an OLRC per-Congress classification table: a U.S. Code place one public law section touched, with the Statutes at Large page and the publisher's action word.
classes.coverage: Sampled. Every row of each public-law-order table the OLRC classification index links for a scoped Congress, read whole every run and replacing that session's rows. The index links the current Congress's session tables only.
classes.data_quality: A row is its position on the page (`seq`), because one line can repeat; a page read this run replaces every prior row for its Congress and session, so a line the publisher removed does not linger under a position it no longer holds. A session not read keeps its rows, and `observed_at` says when they were read. On 2026-10-02 and -03 OLRC answered its classification pages with a maintenance page and status 200, which the reader refuses rather than reading as an empty table. A refused page, or a 401/403, is journaled as `classification-refused` with its URL, status and time, and the nightly `scripts/check_source_refusals.py` fails while the current laws generation holds one; a 401/403 that leaves no session table read also fails the laws run after it publishes. A transport failure is only retried on the next run. Only the public-law order is read: the code-order twin holds the same lines under positions that would collide with these. A Congress the index does not link — every Congress but the current one — gets no rows here; `table3_records` is the historical view. `action` is the page's column 3 verbatim, NULL where the page left it blank, which its legend reads as amended. `usc_section_key` is `usc_section` folded for joins (trimmed, lower-cased, every dash spelling an ASCII hyphen), because case carries no identity in the Code and a join on the printed letter misses the upper-case spellings (decision 30, `docs/research/fork-delivery-decisions-2026-09-22.md`). Every laws run derives `usc_section_key` and `usc_place` again on every row from its stored `usc_section` and `action`, so a session not read keeps current ones; a row meets its `table3_records` record on `law_number` (its `act_key`), title, key and place. A law can be classified in the session table after the one its number suggests (119-70 is in the session-2 table, whose caption names it); filter by `law_id`, not by `session`, and `stated_laws` carries each table's caption.

classes.label: Table III records
classes.summary: One row per classification record of one public law in OLRC's Table III: which U.S. Code place each section of the law went to, as Table III's bulk file states it.
classes.coverage: Window, complete for the Congresses read: every public law Table III holds for each Congress the laws table holds, plus the scoped ones, derived from OLRC's Table III bulk file on each run, so a Congress keeps its rows current after it leaves the laws scope while Table III catches up. The file holds the whole table back to 1789; other Congresses, private laws and pre-1957 session-law chapters are not derived.
classes.data_quality:
Table III holds an act only once OLRC has classified it, and lags enactment: on 2026-09-26 it was current through 119-73, a law of 2026-01-23, while the law route reached 119-111. `release_point` says how current the file was. Its file at release point 119-73 also has no record of 119-70, a second-session law `law_code_sections` classifies (OLRC's gap, not a reading error).
Since 2026-09-26 the rows come from the bulk file (`fulldump@<release point>.xml`) instead of one page per act. The file splits an act's records about ten to an `<act>` fragment. An act's rows are its fragments' records in the file's order, and `seq` is a record's position in its act, as on the page; the file's own `sequence` attribute repeats within 70 acts, so it is not used. Each fragment states its own Congress, date and Statutes volume, and a record carries its fragment's volume where it states a page. Replayed against the 2,981 rows the pages had published, every row keeps its position, act section, Statutes page and volume, Code title and section, status and release point. The file also holds 119-30 and 119-53, whose pages the page walk never reached. Four act-level columns now carry the file's spelling instead of the page's: `stated_key` `119-37` (page `119–37`), `congress` `119` (`119th Cong.`), `act_date` `2025-11-12` (`Nov. 12, 2025`) and `statutes_at_large_volume` `139` (`139 Stat.`).
OLRC states no Last-Modified, ETag or Content-Length for the zip, so each run fetches it; it was byte-identical on 2026-09-14 and 2026-09-26 at the same release point. Each Congress keeps a checkpoint in the file's metadata: the derivation rule with a digest of SpicyDocs' code (not its release string, so a version-only release derives nothing), the member's digest and release point, and each act's shaped-row digest. While all match, nothing is derived. Otherwise every scoped act is derived again, and only an act whose rows changed is published, its whole row set replaced.
Table III only grows: across the eight consecutive releases from 116-150 (2020-07) to 119-73, archived by the Wayback Machine, no act was ever dropped (receipt `table3-bulk-2026-09-26/wayback/`). So a held act the file no longer lists loses its rows only when the release point advances, at most one act a release, and the removal is journaled as `rows-retired` for qualification to reconcile. A file whose release point is older than the one published, that drops an act without advancing, or that drops more than one is refused, and so is a file the reader refuses outright: the member has been renamed twice since 2020. A refused read publishes nothing for this table and keeps every checkpoint, while `laws` and `law_code_sections` publish as usual. The build journals it as `table3-bulk-refused`, and the nightly `scripts/check_source_refusals.py` fails while the current laws generation holds one, so the table cannot stop updating in silence. A transport failure is only retried on the next run. `usc_section_key` is the bare section folded for joins (trimmed, lower-cased, every dash spelling an ASCII hyphen), because case carries no identity in the Code and Table III itself prints some sections both ways (decision 30, `docs/research/fork-delivery-decisions-2026-09-22.md`); the note or preceding words Table III prints inside `usc_section` are in `usc_place` (until 2026-10-03 they stayed in the key, on 1,121 of 2,983 rows). Every laws run derives both again on every row from its stored `usc_section`, so held rows need no read of the file for them.

classes.label: Committees
classes.summary: One row per committee or subcommittee of any Congress the Congress.gov committee list route states, keyed on the publisher's `systemCode`, with the detail record's history, subcommittees, parent and currency folded on where captured.
classes.coverage: Sampled. Since 2026-09-26 the Congress.gov committee route is walked whole with no Congress: every committee of every Congress the publisher records, because `committee_meetings` keeps the previous Congress and `bill_committees` reaches the 108th. The committee detail is folded onto each row under a per-run cap, newest `update_date` first; a committee whose detail was captured is re-read only when its list row's `update_date` moves. Receipt `committee-fixes-2026-09-26/3-rosters-118/`.
classes.data_quality: The route over-declares: on 2026-09-19 `committee/119` declared 238 and served 236 on its one terminal page with no continuation. The reader's terminal-page count refusal is the one refusal this rollup reads past, publishing what the publisher served with both numbers in the run log; every other walk refusal fails the run. `detail_captured` says whether the detail's columns are the publisher's or NULL; where the detail was captured, its `subcommittees` are the row's, an empty list included. The detail's counts (`bill_count` and the rest) are that day's statement, dated by `detail_update_date`. Rows are committees of every Congress: filter `is_current` for today's. 95 historical committees are keyed on their Library of Congress name-authority id (`n79043125`, the Senate's Indian Affairs, 1820-1946), which their history states as `locLinkedDataId`; none is current. A code the detail route cannot address is a list row with `detail_captured` false.

classes.label: Committee assignments
classes.summary: One row per member per committee or subcommittee seat a chamber roster file lists today, from the House Clerk's MemberData.xml and the Senate's cvc_member_data.xml.
classes.coverage: Sampled. Today's seats: the House Clerk's and the Senate's committee files are captured whole each run, for the current Congress only, and each capture replaces its chamber's rows for that Congress; an earlier Congress keeps its last capture. Vacant and placeholder seats appear as the Clerk's file states them.
classes.data_quality: A row is a seat the file listed on its `file_date`: a seat the file no longer lists is gone on the next capture. The House file states its Congress and the reader proves it; the Senate file states none, so its rows carry the caller's Congress with `congress_basis` = `caller`. A House vacancy has no member and no row, and a seated member whose only assignment is the file's `<committee rank=""/>` placeholder has none either (nine placeholders on 2026-09-19). Only a file captured this run replaces its chamber's rows; a chamber whose file was not established keeps its prior rows. House `system_code` derives its prefix from the native committee type and parent context; `committee_code` preserves the literal source identifier. Join matching `system_code` values to `committees` and `bioguide_id` to `members`. Rows whose `system_code` matches no committee stay listed and are never matched by name (the Joint Economic Committee has three Congress.gov codes). On 2026-09-23 that is 28 rows: 25 House seats on the Clerk's four joint committees (`EC00`, `IT00`, `JL00`, `JP00`, typed `joint` in the Clerk file with no Congress.gov code), and three Senate seats on `JSIK00`, the 2024 inaugural committee, which Congress.gov does not list in any Congress.

classes.label: Federal Register documents
classes.summary: One row per dated Federal Register record, keyed by (`document_number`, `publication_date`), ingested from the federalregister.gov REST API by `build_federal_register`. The authoritative rule-publication record — proposed rules, final rules, and notices — complementary to the regulations.gov `dockets`/`documents` view. `regulation_id_numbers` (RIN) and `cfr_references` are the join keys to the Unified Agenda and the CFR.
classes.coverage: True range: dated records published from 1994-01-03 on, the whole span the API serves.
classes.data_quality: Document numbers are not globally unique: `00-111` names different records on 2000-01-14 and 2000-01-18. Current merging preserves both dates and replaces only the same dated record on a later successful fetch. This code correction does not restore historical records already lost from published files; those require a pinned historical replay and publication. A number-only source reference remains ambiguous when its input generation supplies multiple dated candidates. One RIN, docket and title can cover a rule and its later corrections, effective-date delays and confirmations, all typed `Rule` since 2008 with `subtype` NULL, so a RIN or title match picks a document family, not a document; `action` tells them apart (`Final rule; correction.`) where the Register states one. The API lists no RIN on a large share of `Rule` documents every year, some of which state one in the printed text or inside `docket_ids`. A row not read since the Register's regulations.gov link and `action` were first requested (2026-10-03) is NULL in all nine of those columns, which means not read: test `regulations_dot_gov_info_json`, which a row read since holds as `'{}'` at least. The scheduled run re-reads the last 120 days, so a relayed comment count follows the Register's own checks to about the comment period's close.

classes.label: FEC committees by cycle
classes.summary: One row per FEC committee per two-year cycle, as that cycle's bulk committee master states it: name, treasurer, address, designation, type, party, filing frequency, interest-group category, connected organization and linked candidate. Read by the `fec-committee-history` rollup through SpicyDocs' committee-master reader, which verifies each file by digest and checks the publisher's header. Codes stay literal. `fec_committees` is the current registry from the API; this is the history, keyed on (`committee_id`, `cycle`).
classes.coverage: True range. Every cycle from 1980 through the current one: each run reads every cycle's bulk committee master whole and publishes every row. The current cycle's file is republished daily, so its rows change.

classes.label: FEC candidates by cycle

classes.label: House executive communications
classes.summary: One row per House executive communication, as the Congress.gov house-communication list and detail routes state it, keyed on the publisher's own address. The regulatory bridge: `is_rulemaking`, the cited `legal_authority`, the committee referral, the matching House requirement and the RIN read from `report_nature`. A Federal Register RIN join must unnest `regulation_id_numbers` (the scalar `federal_register.rin` is the first value only) and retain number plus publication date. The Register API lists no RIN on many `Rule` documents, including some whose printed text states one, and sometimes prints the RIN inside `docket_ids`, so a RIN join misses those and can land on a correction or effective-date notice that shares the rule's RIN, docket and title; `federal_register.action` tells such a notice from its rule.
classes.coverage: Window: the sitting Congress (the 119th), every communication the Congress.gov house-communication list declares for each type (`ec`, `ml`, `pm`, `pt`), the list walked whole each run and refused short of the publisher's declared total, with every detail read. A later run reads new details newest first under its per-run cap, so a row it has not reached is list-only (`detail_read` false), not absent. The output ledger records the declared counts beside what is held.
classes.data_quality: A row whose `detail_read` is `false` is list-only: its detail has not been read yet (not reached under the cap, or refused), and every detail-only column is NULL with it, including the scalar and occurrence RIN columns, because the rule was not run. A read detail's list is `[]` where the detail states an empty one and NULL where it states none. Rows read before spicy-docs 0.54.0 spelled both `[]`; each such row is read once more (817 on 2026-10-03, one run). The RIN is an interpretation: `rin_rule` names the rule that fired (`report_nature_rin_label/2`) or `unmatched`, and `rin_matched_text` is the exact text, so a false positive is readable from the row. Every run derives the four RIN columns of each read row again from its retained `report_nature`, re-read or not, so no row keeps an earlier SpicyDocs' scalar or rule name. The rows the `rin_rule` column note says name `report_nature_rin_label` last only until this table's first run under SpicyDocs 0.50.1: after it, no row names the old rule. The publisher repeats a record across a page boundary; the table holds each identity once. The shared pooled list reader must settle each query by distinct identity before any output is replaced. Every existing publisher row receives source_route=congress-gov-detail. Bounded reads of selected Congressional Record issues can fill record_package_id, record_granule_id and record_entry_text from exactly one printed entry with matching Congress, communication type and number. Missing, repeated or incompletely read entries leave these fields empty. The source receipts distinguish unread, failed, empty and ambiguous results. API observations and source_route remain unchanged. Submitting-official and submitting-agency values are not inferred from the printed text.

classes.label: Committee meetings
classes.summary: One scheduled committee meeting, keyed by Congress, chamber and event ID. Detail fields preserve independently listed committees, bills, nominations, treaties, hearing jackets, witnesses and document URLs. Hearing references require Congress and chamber context; document URLs do not prove acquisition.
classes.coverage: Sampled, and accumulating. Congress.gov meeting lists cover the current Congress and updates to the previous Congress. New meeting details are read newest first, at most 1,000 a run. Unread or refused details leave list-only records. The previous Congress remains in scope because published transcripts can update its meetings.
classes.data_quality:
A row whose `detail_read` is `false` is list-only: its detail has not been read yet, and every detail-only column is NULL with it. A read detail's list is `[]` where the detail states an empty one and NULL where it states none. Rows read before spicy-docs 0.54.0 spelled both `[]`; each such row is read once more, after a run's own reads and under its cap of 1,000, and until then its `[]` can mean either. Event ids are keyed with their chamber because their uniqueness across chambers is unmeasured (spicy-docs' contract note); the 119th's House and Senate event ids come from different ranges, so an id alone does not say which chamber. The publisher's witness entries can repeat within one meeting, so count people by name, not entries.
**Related bills.** Congress.gov often leaves the related bills off a markup's detail, so `bill_ids_json` names none; the meeting's documents usually still name them, in a `meeting_documents_json` entry whose `documentType` is `Bills and Resolutions`. A bill named only in a meeting document is not in `bill_ids_json`.
**A meeting can carry no committee**: `committee_system_code` and `committees_json` are NULL where the detail names none (Senate Finance's nominations meeting of 2026-07-23, event 338678), so a filter on the committee misses it; search `title` as well. **`meeting_status` is Congress.gov's and can lag**: a hearing the committee rescheduled can stay `Scheduled` under its first date (Senate Finance's trade-agenda hearing, event 338326 on 2026-04-23, which the committee lists as rescheduled to July, event 338681).
**Senate and NoChamber meetings list no witnesses here.** Congress.gov's committee-meeting detail, the route this table reads, has no `witnesses` element for those chambers (retained detail `119/nochamber/338692`), so their witness lists are `[]` or NULL: the route stated none, not that the meeting had none. For a printed hearing, `hearing_transcripts.witnesses_json` lists the witnesses GovInfo's MODS names (CHRG-119shrg64653 names four). A transcript reaches its meeting by `event_id`, or by `mods_event_id` where `event_id` is NULL, with `congress` and `chamber`; most Senate transcripts name no meeting either way, so most Senate meetings have no witness list from either source.
The publisher's `NoChamber` value is stored as `nochamber`, matching its detail address and preserving the existing row identity. It is neither NULL nor an inferred `joint` chamber. The source reader accepts that address, so previously list-only rows can fill at an unchanged timestamp. Retained meeting `119/nochamber/338692` names the Helsinki Commission; the September 24 committee-meetings audit retains its list row and served detail.

classes.label: Daily Congressional Record issues
classes.summary: One row per daily Congressional Record issue, keyed `(volume, issue)`, the publisher's own identity. The detail's section names give `chambers`, the legislative-day calendar (which chambers sat), and the stem of the whole-issue link for part 1 gives the GovInfo CREC `package_id` (`entire_issue_url_stem/2`). The volume is the year minus 1854 (volume 172 is 2026).
classes.coverage: Sampled, and accumulating. Each run walks the whole `daily-congressional-record/{volume}` list for each session volume of the Congresses in scope and reads the detail of every issue the table does not yet hold, newest `updateDate` first, up to 1,000 a run, so at the 119th's size one run completes it.
classes.data_quality: A row whose `detail_read` is `false` is list-only: its detail has not been read yet, so `chambers`, `package_id` and every other detail-only column are NULL with it. A read detail with no chamber section (a Daily Digest only) states an empty `chambers`, distinct from NULL. The rule before 2026-09-29 read the first whole-issue link listed, and an issue printed in several books lists a later book's `-bk{N}` link first on 7 of 368 held rows, which GovInfo holds no package under; a one-time rebuild re-reads every held row's own `entire_issue` under the new rule.

classes.label: Treaty documents
classes.summary: One treaty document, identified by received Congress, number and suffix. An unpartitioned document may have a derived GovInfo CDOC package ID; that locator does not prove the package has been published or acquired. Related documents, titles and countries remain source-stated lists.
classes.coverage: Sampled. Retained 119th-Congress treaty list records and available details. Excludes treaty bodies, action histories, older Congresses, suffixed-part details and interpreted legal effects. Incoming references retain the treaty's received Congress and partition.
classes.data_quality: Partitioned treaties remain list-only because the maintained source reader has no suffixed detail route. Their derived package ID is NULL. Whether an unpartitioned detail was read is recorded in its source evidence; a list record alone does not establish available treaty text.

classes.label: Nominations
classes.summary: One row per nomination or part, as the Congress.gov nomination list route states it, keyed `(congress, citation)`; the citation carries the part number.
classes.coverage: Sampled. Retained 119th-Congress nomination-list identities, including partitioned nominations. Repeated list entries mean pagination totals alone do not prove completeness. Optional committee and hearing lists are recorded only after their relationship reads complete. Read outcomes distinguish unread, failed and successfully empty responses. Latest actions are retained; full action histories, person identities and inferred confirmation outcomes are outside scope.
classes.data_quality: List walks retain each complete Congress/citation identity and newest source update, including partitions. Inconsistent or incomplete walks fail before replacing outputs. Committee and hearing lists are independent: NULL is unread or unstated, while an empty list records a complete empty response. Civilian/military classification uses retained source flags; it does not infer confirmation.

classes.label: Committee activity reports (House and Senate)
classes.summary: One row per captured end-of-Congress committee activity report package, House or Senate (the table's name predates its Senate rows; the package id's `hrpt`/`srpt` says which), with what its print adds to its own MODS index. Joins `document_citations` on `package_id` = `document_key` and `text_sha256`.
classes.coverage: Sampled. House committee activity reports: CRPT packages from the 2023-01-01 issue floor whose titles name activity under the shared title rule. Not an earlier-archive census.
classes.data_quality: **The MODS is authoritative for bills, laws and Code sections, and this table's own columns say so.** Read at full page depth across the eight reports spicy-docs sampled, the print named 0 of 1,406 bills, 0 of 174 public laws, 0 of 37 U.S. Code sections and 0 of 7 Statutes at Large pages that the package MODS does not already state — so `distinct_bills_beyond_index`, `distinct_laws_beyond_index` and `distinct_usc_sections_beyond_index` are near zero, and a nonzero one is worth reading the evidence span for rather than taking as new yield. Measured here 2026-09-20 over **41** reports rather than eight, "zero" is very nearly right and not exactly right: 7 print-only bills of 7,686 distinct, 5 print-only laws of 990, and 6 print-only Code sections. The one apparent survivor, `188-11`, was the print's own misprint of `118-11`. What the print does add is committees beyond the submitting one (27 resolved codes), 87 RINs, 38 agency dockets and 5 GAO product ids. **Except for the Congress of a Senate report's bills.** A Senate committee files its report early in the following Congress, and GovInfo stamps the MODS's bills with that filing Congress; printed bills are keyed in `covered_congress`, the Congress the report itself states, so on a Senate report `bills_congress_mismatch` and `distinct_bills_beyond_index` count the MODS's wrong Congress, not new yield (2026-09-26 drift audit: the eight Senate reports on the 117th had published 1,915 citations under 118th-Congress bills before the fix). **And for a House report's bills printed under a Congress subheading.** CRPT-117hrpt705 and -118hrpt974 print a predecessor bill's history under `116th Congress` or `117th Congress` inside the current bill's entry, and -118hrpt967 heads each Congress of its committee history, 107th to 118th, the same way; since spicy-docs `bill_number` 004 those bills are keyed in the subheading's Congress until the next entry, while the MODS stamps them with the filing one, so `bills_congress_mismatch` and `distinct_bills_beyond_index` count them (45 on -117hrpt705, 225 on -118hrpt967; replay receipt `print-subheading-2026-09-26/`). Since `bill_number` 005 a bill the print sets its own Congress beside (`H.R. 6752, 115th Cong.`, `S. Res. 116, 112th Congress`) takes that one ahead of any subheading, and those count the same way (38 citations over the 40 reports; receipt `print-inline-congress-2026-09-26/`). A committee name both chambers hold (`Committee on the Judiciary`, `on the Budget`, `on Veterans' Affairs`, `on Armed Services`, `on Appropriations`) resolves to the chamber of the report's own committee, read off the package id; before 2026-09-26 the House won every such name, and the Senate reports published 1,746 House codes for their own committees, 1,718 of them `hsju00`. A chamber the print names before a committee (`Senate Committee on Armed Services`) selects that chamber's committees instead (76 rows moved, 24 of them `hshm00` to `ssga00`). **Limit:** 7 bare committee names in Senate reports reach a name only the House roster holds and keep the House's code, because the print names no chamber: 5 `hshm00` (a wrapped `Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs`, or its `Committee on Home-` fragment) and 2 `hsso00` (`Select Committee on Ethics`). Read them as ambiguous, not as House committees. Receipt: `fix-print-citations-2026-09-26/replay-qualified.json`. `committees_unresolved` is **a floor, not a defect count**: the Senate `cvc` roster states only the committees its listed senators sit on, so a name it does not reach stays unresolved rather than being guessed. `stated_page_count` is the publisher's own `pages` field and is never re-derived from the bytes; `pages_read` is what the extraction saw, and the two are reported separately on purpose (CRPT-118hrpt965 states 282 and a 60-page read saw 60). `submitted_by_bioguide_id` is NULL where the publisher states the member without an id, which CRPT-118hrpt965 does.

classes.label: President's budget volumes
classes.summary: One row per published volume of the President's budget, with what its print adds to its own MODS index. Thirteen measured package parts are accepted; only volumes offering a supported package-root body yield rows.
classes.coverage: Sampled. BUDGET packages from the 2023-01-01 issue floor whose root PDF follows the provider's thirteen-part grammar, read under a per-run package cap. TAB, DB, CLIMATE and LRB have no root PDF; no granule route is attempted.
classes.data_quality:
**The bill counts are congress-blind and are not join keys.** A BUDGET package states no Congress anywhere — not in its id, not in its summary — so the print can only spell `HR7806` where the MODS states `119-hr-7806`. `distinct_bills` and `distinct_bills_beyond_index_congress_blind` therefore reduce **both** sides to `{bill_type}-{number}` before comparing, which is why the column carries `congress_blind` in its name; neither can join `congress_bills.bill_id`, which needs the Congress this family never states. For the same reason the per-row `stated_by_index` on a `bill_number` citation of a budget volume is **NULL, not `false`**: the comparison was not possible, and answering `false` would report a comparison nobody made. Measured across the eight volumes spicy-docs sampled at full page depth, 6 of the 8 distinct printed bills are print-only. The family's real yield is laws: **504 of 518** distinct public laws the prints name are absent from their own MODS at full page depth, against 43 of 69 at a 60-page cap. `fiscal_year` is not the issue year — `BUDGET-2026-MSR` was issued 2025-09-05 — and is stated twice, by the package id and by the MODS, which spicy-docs asserts agree. `associated_bills` is published whole because it is the only statement of this edge that carries a Congress.

**Thirteen measured parts are accepted by spicy-docs 0.24.0.** The seven additions are `OBJCLASS`, `TAB`, `DB`, `CLIMATE`, `LRB`, `CROSSCUT` and `DOD`. On one measured volume per part, `TAB`, `DB` and `CLIMATE` offer PDF only at granule stems; `LRB` offers an XLS and no supported body. A `GovInfoFormatNotOfferedError` at the package root is counted and logged as the publisher's answer, not as a failed or missing volume. No granule route is attempted: `shape_budget_volume` takes package summary/MODS and does not support a granule identity. These observations remain eligible on the next run and produce no invented document row.

classes.label: Committee-print bill actions
classes.summary: One row per action phrase a committee print states about one bill it names in the same sentence: the print's own phrasing, the sealed stage and BILLSTATUS action codes it maps to, and how reliable the pairing is. Joins `document_citations` through `document_key`, `text_sha256` and `mention_span_start` = `span_start`.
classes.coverage: Derived: the committee actions printed in the accepted House activity reports (`house_activity_reports`), not all committee actions.
classes.data_quality: **These are rule-derived interpretations with measured errors.** `attachment_confidence` is `single` where the sentence names one bill and `multi` where it names several. Hand-checked over 60 mentions by spicy-docs: a `single` row is both the right kind of action and the right bill **83.3 percent** of the time (30 of 36), a `multi` row **50 percent** (2 of 4). `WHERE attachment_confidence = 'single'` selects the class with higher measured precision, at an 8 percent volume cost in that sample (4,089 of 4,456 rows were `single`). It does not qualify an individual row as correct. The vendored column description below still says "hosted-quality"; that wording is superseded by these limits and awaits adoption of the corrected source package. `multi` rows are kept rather than dropped because `sentence_start`, `sentence_end` and `matched_text` make them readable, and `bills_in_sentence` is published raw so a consumer can set its own threshold. **Precision is not recall: recall is 59.6 percent**, re-weighted by stratum over 148 checked contexts. The print writes "the bill" after naming it once, sets an en-bloc disposition as a sentence about "the measures", and states a committee consideration date in a ruled table's column header — so a consumer counting hearings from these rows is counting a floor. `sealed_stage` is **NULL on 1,670 of 4,456 rows** and that is a finding rather than a gap: a rung is never invented, so `passed the House` stays NULL rather than widening the sealed `passed house` matcher. spicy-docs 0.51.0 reads these phrases through its new stage rules on the next print-citations build: over the 12,695 live rows of 2026-09-29, 2,058 `referred` rows move from `other_chamber` to `committee`, and 476 rows staged `law` by a phrase that merely contains "public law" become NULL, since the became-law matcher must now start the phrase (5,245 NULL become 5,721; spicy-docs' own `sealed_stage` over each row's `matched_text`). `billstatus_action_code` is NULL on 280 rows whose phrasing has no known code at all (`vetoed`, `not_considered`, `declined_markup`, `favorably_forwarded`, `included_in`), and a further 639 rows are coded through codes the publisher's own retained guide never lists — 13 of the 35 distinct codes in the retained responses appear nowhere in its action-code table, which the guide itself says is representational rather than authoritative. `stated_date` is extracted and published but **was never scored**: nothing establishes that the date the sentence states belongs to this action. On a 20-bill probe the publisher had no counterpart at all to 10 of the 15 subcommittee hearings these prints state, while all 8 markups were stated and coded — which is what this table is for.

classes.label: Document citation link table
classes.summary: One cited target occurrence in one version of a document's text, retaining the cited key, exact matched text and character span. Repeated mentions stay separate. Citation kinds include bills, laws, RINs, dockets and GAO products. Read outcomes distinguish successful zero findings from missing evidence.
classes.coverage: Derived, and selective. Citation occurrences from held House activity reports and budget volumes, plus operator-selected fields from bills, reports, lobbying records, comments, communications and court opinions, at most 100 selected fields per run. `document_citation_read_outcomes` records exact read scopes and successful zero findings. No citation rows can mean unread, refused or no matches; this table is not an inventory of held text. Page-read evidence belongs to receipts, not the main report or budget columns.
classes.data_quality:
**The span is in the identity because the span is the yield.** Keying on document, kind and target alone would collapse CRPT-118hrpt968's repeated mentions of one bill into one row; the aggregate is derivable from this table with `GROUP BY document_key, cite_kind, target_key` and the reverse is not. **Different text digests retain their histories.** A source revision producing a new `text_sha256` adds findings beside earlier text versions. A successful rule correction for the same document and text digest replaces that digest's findings, including an empty result; it can retire obsolete rows. A failed read preserves previous findings. Size grows with retained text revisions and their citations. Filter to the digest the document row states (`house_activity_reports.text_sha256` or `budget_volumes.text_sha256`) to read exactly one extraction. Prints are revised rarely, so this is a property to know before building on the table; pruning earlier text digests would require a separate retention decision. `stated_by_index` is three-valued and the third value matters: `true`/`false` where a keyed index record was read and could state a key of this shape, and **NULL where no comparison was possible** — either no index record was supplied or the MODS vocabulary has no element of that shape, which is the case for every bill citation of a budget volume. So the consumer predicate for "what the print adds" is `WHERE stated_by_index IS NOT TRUE`, never `= false`. `target_resolved` false means the cite was found and its key is unsettled, not that the cite is wrong. `target_rule` says **how** a key was reached and separates lookups from inferences: `exact` and `roster_prefix` are lookups against a supplied vocabulary, while `name_prefix` and `sibling_prefix` are inferences from the printed text that a consumer may decline. `evidence_page` is NULL where the rendition states no page boundary, and a match straddling a page break is attributed to the page it began on.
**A document with no rows here is not shown to be unheld.** Each held-field kind has rows only for the documents selected so far (on 2026-10-03 the report_section rows covered one of the report packages `report_sections` holds); count distinct `document_key` by `document_kind` for the live figure. GAO product ids join `gao_reports` on `report_number = target_key`, GAO's own spelling (`report_id` is the same id in lower case); the few that do not resolve are `…SU` products, which `gao_reports` does not hold, and misprints such as `GAO-21-105520` (GAO-23-105520 is held).

classes.label: Secretary of the Senate expenditure tables
classes.summary: One printed expenditure row, retaining cells and their stated header roles. Identity includes package, file, page, table, row and body version. A package has separate Part I and Part II files that repeat some summary pages; package ID alone is not a record key.
classes.coverage: Sampled. GovInfo CDOC expenditure reports from the 2024-01-01 issue floor, limited by a per-run package cap and the first 80 pages of each file. Counts are lower bounds. Part I and Part II repeat summary pages before diverging into detailed statements. The later compensation and mail-allocation sections lie outside this page window. Page-limit evidence is retained separately from the printed main rows.
classes.data_quality:
**Most rows carry one cell, not a row of cells, and `cells_ruled` is how you tell.** Of the ruled body rows across the pages spicy-docs measured when it wrote the contract (release 0.23.0), those in an `appropriation_summary` grid carry all nine cells and every other one carries exactly **one** cell of ten or of seven: the print rules a whole payee block as a single cell. That is why the contract has no `payee_name`, `document_number`, `date_posted` or singular `amount` column — those would be a parse of one cell's newlines presented as separate facts. `WHERE cells_ruled` selects the rows whose cells are separate facts; everything else is in `cells` exactly as printed. **`cells` is the row**; every other content column is a promotion out of it. `office`, `funding_year`, `appropriation_title` and `section_heading` are read from the page text and are **NULL on a continuation page**, which is 56 of the 139 measured table pages — forward-fill them in `printed_page` order. `printed_page`, not `page`, is what the report's own contents index by. `grid_kind` is NULL where the first row states none of the three known labels, so an unrecognised grid is visible rather than mislabelled. An amount must carry a decimal point to be parsed into `amounts`: without that rule a bare integer read stacked fiscal years and account numbers as money, and every amount-shaped line measured carries a `.dd` tail while the lines that do not are all account numbers or fiscal years. The check that makes the extraction falsifiable is the print's own `Totals` row, which agreed to the cent with the sum of its account rows over seven money columns on both measured sections.
**What each package's read window holds.** Part I's pages reach the `A-` summary and the leadership and officers' `B-` pages; Part II's reach a short alphabetical run of senators' offices (in GPO-CDOC-119sdoc6: Justice, Kaine, Kelly and Kennedy), so a Senate-wide or other senator's figure is not here; `SELECT DISTINCT office` for the package says which offices are. The `A-` summary is by appropriation account only, with no object-class (travel and the like) rollup: object classes are in each office's `ORGANIZATION TOTALS` block. One report period's spending is spread over one block per funding year (FY2024, FY2025 and FY2026 in the October 2025 to March 2026 report), so sum the blocks' period amounts. A zero prints as `$.00`.
A payroll cell can interleave two printed lines letter by letter ("D SEIR NE AC TT OO RR" for DIRECTOR and SENATOR, on GPO-CDOC-119sdoc5-2 page B-1470 and 119sdoc6-2 page B-1262), so the cells hold the print exactly for the amounts, which stayed intact, and not always for the text.

classes.label: Native legal-reference observations
classes.summary: Original legal references and source passages with recorded target matches. Inspect every candidate's complete keys, target pin, match count and reason. Found, missing, ambiguous, unsupported and not-checked remain separate. Source paths and interpretation rules stay visible. A complete read replaces its selected source/edition scope, including a successful empty correction. U.S. Code section matches identify held classification rows, not Code text.
classes.coverage: Sampled. Selected retained U.S. Code and eCFR XML inputs only. Read scopes state the edition, input digest and forms checked; they do not establish source-wide completeness.

classes.label: Legal reference read scopes
classes.summary: Each input's latest completed read, including reads that found no observations. Shows exact source scope, edition, XML and selection-manifest digests, byte and observation counts, forms checked and forms left out. Failed or incomplete inputs cannot replace prior results.
classes.coverage: Not a range. Completed reads of selected retained XML inputs; absent scopes remain unknown.

classes.label: GAO recommendations
classes.summary: One recommendation per agency, retaining GAO's last-listed text, status, priority and progress comments. Daily validated export reads accumulate records rather than delete them. Identity uses product, kind, agency and stated recommendation number, or text when unnumbered. `report_id` connects its product. `listed_open=false` means absent from the latest export; closure, edits or reassignment may explain it. Priority counts are limited by this observation window. Director phone numbers are removed from retained evidence.
classes.coverage: Window. Daily whole reads of GAO's open-recommendations export, including recommendations on products issued from 2001 onward. Coverage starts at `min(first_seen)`; earlier closures never appear. Entries leaving the export remain with `listed_open=false` and their last-seen date. Removal does not state a closure reason. `first_seen` records when this table observed the recommendation open, not when GAO made it.

classes.label: Bill vote references
classes.summary: One row per recorded vote on one bill action: which roll call the bill's own actions say settled it. Read by the `roll-call-votes` rollup to fill `roll_call_votes.bill_id` and its match columns.

classes.label: Court opinion texts (Markdown)
classes.summary: Each CourtListener opinion's text as Markdown in the GitHub Flavored Markdown dialect with footnotes ([^n] references and definitions), its citations as links [cite](opinion:ID) to the cited opinion_id. Join opinion_id to court_opinions and cluster_id to court_opinion_clusters (court_is_federal selects federal courts). An opinion without text has a row with text_source 'none' and NULL markdown; where a PDF of it was extracted, court_opinion_pdf_extractions joins it by opinion_id. Stored id sorted, one file per block of 150,000 opinion ids (opinion_block is opinion_id // 150000): route a point read through the publication index, whose court_opinion_texts entry lists each file with its opinion_block, and read that one file (4 HTTP range requests measured). A filter on opinion_id alone over every file is the slow path: it opens each file's footer (154 requests over 75 files measured). opinion_id is text, so filter it with a quoted literal (opinion_id = '123'); an unquoted number casts every row, so no row group is skipped (105 requests against 4 on one file of 102 row groups). Rows are in numeric id order within a file; ORDER BY opinion_id sorts as text, so order by CAST(opinion_id AS BIGINT). Receipts point at the export (its SHA-256), the opinion id, the export column converted and the SHA-256 of that column's value, not a copy of it.
classes.coverage: Not a range. Not published: only a bounded build of the head of the 2026-06-30 CourtListener opinions export has run; it proves the build path and establishes no completeness. Every opinion of an export gets a row, federal or not; select federal courts by joining cluster_id to court_opinion_clusters and filtering court_is_federal.
classes.data_quality: The text is converted from the publisher's html_with_citations, else html, else plain_text (in the whole 2026-06-30 export 9,355 opinions fall back to html, 7,976 to plain_text and 554 have no text); images are dropped. Preformatted bodies (a fifth of the export) keep their line breaks and indentation. Accepted fidelity (owner, 2026-10-31): no citation link, heading, blockquote or paragraph lost; footnotes and italics at most 0.5% lost; tables at most 1%. On 500 sampled opinions stratified by source rendering, all 5,539 citation links kept their cited id and text, and no heading, blockquote or table was lost; 0.28% of italic characters were. All 394 referenced footnote bodies read back as footnote definitions and the 6 bodies nothing references stay in place as text; 2 markers point at bodies the rendering does not contain. A plain CommonMark reader misreads footnote definitions; read with a GFM parser that supports footnotes.
